1: # Segmented Campus Network - GNS3 Build Kit
2: 
3: A complete, paste-ready GNS3 lab for:
4: 
5: - **2 routers** (R1 campus gateway/firewall/DHCP/NAT, R2 simulated ISP)
6: - **3 switches** (SW1 distribution, SW2 staff/student access, SW3 guest/IoT access)
7: - **STAFF VLAN** with 3 Docker clients
8: - **STUDENT VLAN** with 3 Docker clients
9: - **GUEST VLAN** with 1 Docker client
10: - **IOT VLAN** with 3 real Docker sensors publishing MQTT
11: - **Firewall policy** as five named extended ACLs on R1
12: - **RADIUS dynamic VLAN** using FreeRADIUS and 802.1X for users (MAB-ready
13:   RADIUS entries for sensors)
14: - **MQTT broker** and a server segment isolated behind R1
15: 
16: The lab was built and run end to end in GNS3 3.1 with IOSv/IOSvL2 images:
17: 802.1X dynamic VLAN assignment, DHCP, MQTT, the ACL matrices and NAT were
18: exercised and the captured output is in `report/evidence/`. See
19: [Live validation performed](#live-validation-performed-gns3-31-iosviiosvl2)
20: for the results and the one platform gap (MAB on IOSvL2).
21: 
22: ## What you must supply
23: 
24: 1. **Cisco IOSv image** for R1 and R2 (IOS 15.x, at least 3 GigabitEthernet
25:    interfaces). Import it into GNS3 as an IOSv QEMU template.
26: 2. **Cisco IOSvL2 image** for SW1, SW2, SW3 (IOS 15.2-class, at least 8
27:    GigabitEthernet interfaces, 802.1X-capable feature set). Import it as an
28:    IOSvL2 QEMU template and mark it as an Ethernet switch.
29: 3. **GNS3 2.2.x** with a local Linux server (or a GNS3 VM with Docker).
30: 4. **Docker Engine + Compose v2** on the GNS3 server host, for FreeRADIUS,
31:    Mosquitto and the endpoint images.
32: 
33: The Cisco images are **not** included and cannot be redistributed here. No
34: image filenames are assumed: use whatever IOSv/IOSvL2 images you are licensed
35: to use, then match the interface names in the configs.
36: 
37: You do **not** need Packet Tracer. Packet Tracer cannot do this lab's RADIUS
38: dynamic VLAN and MAB behavior; use GNS3 or EVE-NG.
39: 
40: ## Repository layout
41: 
42: ```
43: network-project/
44:   README.md                       this file
45:   topology/
46:     topology.md                   diagram, port map, addressing
47:     gns3-build-steps.md           click-by-click GNS3 build and paste order
48:   configs/
49:     R1.cfg R2.cfg                 routers
50:     SW1.cfg SW2.cfg SW3.cfg       switches
51:   radius/
52:     docker-compose.yml            FreeRADIUS + Mosquitto on the server segment
53:     clients.conf                  SW1/SW2/SW3 RADIUS clients + secret
54:     users                         users, MAC users, Tunnel-* VLAN attributes
55:     secrets.env                   canonical list of lab secrets/placeholders
56:     mosquitto.conf                lab broker (anonymous, port 1883)
57:     setup-server-bridge.sh        br-srv + veth + macvlan plumbing
58:   endpoints/
59:     sensor/                       Dockerfile, sensor.py, DHCP/entrypoint
60:     client/                       Dockerfile, wpa_supplicant-*.conf, entrypoint
61:   tests/
62:     test-plan.md                  20 tests, expected results, evidence
63:     verify_configs.py             offline consistency checker
64:   report/
65:     report-outline.md             report sections and screenshot checklist
66:     evidence/                     test screenshots and copied console output
67: ```
68: 
69: ## First 10 minutes
70: 
71: Run these in order. Stop and fix any error before building the GNS3 topology.
72: 
73: ### 1. Check the generated files
74: 
75: ```sh
76: cd network-project
77: python3 tests/verify_configs.py
78: ```
79: 
80: Expected last line: `SUMMARY: ... 0 failed`.
81: 
82: ### 2. Prepare the Docker server segment
83: 
84: ```sh
85: cd radius
86: chmod +x setup-server-bridge.sh
87: ./setup-server-bridge.sh
88: docker compose up -d
89: docker compose ps
90: docker logs radius --tail 30
91: ```
92: 
93: Wait for `Ready to process requests` in the FreeRADIUS log. The script creates
94: `br-srv` and the `srv-mac`/`srv-br` veth pair. The GNS3 Cloud node attaches to
95: `br-srv`; R1 g0/1 connects to that Cloud. R1 is `192.168.50.1` and is the
96: containers' default gateway.
97: 
98: If GNS3 runs inside a **GNS3 VM**, do this inside the VM and attach the Cloud
99: node to the VM's `br-srv`. A local GNS3 server on the same Linux host is the
100: simplest setup. Do not run Compose on your desktop while GNS3 runs in a VM that
101: cannot see that bridge.
102: 
103: ### 3. Build endpoint images
104: 
105: ```sh
106: cd ..            # back to network-project/
107: docker build -t campus-client:1.0 endpoints/client
108: docker build -t campus-sensor:1.0 endpoints/sensor
109: ```
110: 
111: ### 4. Build the GNS3 project
112: 
113: Follow [topology/gns3-build-steps.md](topology/gns3-build-steps.md). It has the
114: node list, 15 links, Docker environment variables, startup order and the exact
115: paste procedure.
116: 
117: Recommended startup order: **RADIUS/MQTT -> SW1/SW2/SW3 -> R1/R2 -> endpoints**.
118: 
119: Recommended config paste order: **SW1 -> SW2 -> SW3 -> R1 -> R2**, ending each
120: with `end` and `write memory`.
121: 
122: ### 5. Run the tests
123: 
124: Use [tests/test-plan.md](tests/test-plan.md). The minimum evidence set is in
125: [report/report-outline.md](report/report-outline.md#screenshot-checklist-minimum).
126: 
127: ## Design summary
128: 
129: | Item | Value |
130: |---|---|
131: | R1-SW1 link | 802.1Q trunk, VLANs 10,20,30,40,99 |
132: | SW1-SW2, SW1-SW3 | 802.1Q trunks, same VLAN list |
133: | Staff | VLAN 10, 192.168.10.0/24, 802.1X, 3 clients |
134: | Student | VLAN 20, 192.168.20.0/24, 802.1X, 3 clients |
135: | Guest | VLAN 30, 192.168.30.0/24, 802.1X + fallback, 1 client |
136: | IoT | VLAN 40, 192.168.40.0/24, port security (MAB on hardware), 3 sensors |
137: | MGMT | VLAN 99, 192.168.99.0/24, SW1 .11/SW2 .12/SW3 .13 |
138: | Server segment | 192.168.50.0/24, RADIUS .10, MQTT .20, R1 .1 |
139: | R1-R2 | 10.0.0.0/30, R1 .1, R2 .2 |
140: | Internet sim | 8.8.8.8/32 on R2 Loopback0 |
141: | DHCP | R1 pools for 10/20/30/40, leases from .21 |
142: | NAT | PAT of 10/20/30/40 out R1 g0/2; server and MGMT not translated |
143: | Firewall | `STAFF_IN`, `STUDENT_IN`, `GUEST_IN`, `IOT_IN`, `MGMT_IN`, inbound on R1 subinterfaces |
144: | RADIUS | FreeRADIUS 3.2.3, EAP-MD5 for users, named group `CAMPUS-RADIUS`, dynamic VLAN via Tunnel-* attributes; MAB identities present for hardware use |
145: 
146: ## Secrets and consistency
147: 
148: `radius/secrets.env` is the canonical list, but Cisco IOS and FreeRADIUS cannot
149: read it directly, so values are repeated in the files they configure. Before
150: using the lab outside an isolated GNS3 project, change:
151: 
152: | Secret | Where it appears |
153: |---|---|
154: | `RADIUS_SECRET` | `radius/secrets.env`, `radius/clients.conf` (4 clients), `configs/SW1.cfg`, `SW2.cfg`, `SW3.cfg` (`key 0 ...`) |
155: | `DEVICE_ENABLE_SECRET` | `radius/secrets.env`, `enable secret` and `username admin ... secret` in all five Cisco configs |
156: | Staff/student/guest passwords | `radius/secrets.env`, `radius/users`, `endpoints/client/wpa_supplicant-*.conf` |
157: | Sensor MACs | `radius/secrets.env`, `radius/users`, GNS3 Docker node MAC / `SENSOR_MAC` |
158: 
159: The checked-in value `S3cr3t-Shared-Key-2026` is a **placeholder shared
160: secret**; it is intentionally easy to find. `tests/verify_configs.py` checks
161: that the copies stay in sync but does not judge their strength.
162: 
163: Do not commit real production secrets. Do not expose the lab's anonymous MQTT
164: broker or RADIUS shared secret outside the isolated lab network.
165: 
166: ## RADIUS authentication choice
167: 
168: Users authenticate with **EAP-MD5**. The stock FreeRADIUS 3.2 image enables
169: `default_eap_type = md5` and needs no client certificate, so the lab is
170: reproducible without a PKI. `wpa_supplicant` is started with the wired driver:
171: `wpa_supplicant -i eth0 -D wired -c <profile>`. The sensor and client
172: entrypoints request DHCP after authentication.
173: 
174: For PEAP/MSCHAPv2 or EAP-TLS, add a CA/server certificate, set `eap=PEAP` and
175: `phase2="auth=MSCHAPV2"` (or `eap=TLS`) in the supplicant profiles, and update
176: the FreeRADIUS `eap` module. EAP-MD5 is deprecated for production Wi-Fi but is
177: appropriate for this wired lab.
178: 
179: ## Live validation performed (GNS3 3.1, IOSv/IOSvL2)
180: 
181: The project `campus-network` was built in GNS3 3.1 with 16 nodes and 15 links
182: and run on a local server. Every device and endpoint was started from the
183: saved project. Highlights:
184: 
185: | Area | What was observed | Result |
186: |---|---|---|
187: | Topology | 3 switches, 2 routers, 7 clients, 3 sensors, Cloud; CDP shows R1-SW1, R1-R2, SW1-SW2, SW1-SW3 | Pass |
188: | Trunks | SW1 `Gi0/0-2` trunking, allowed `10,20,30,40,99`; SW2/SW3 `Gi0/0` the same | Pass |
189: | DHCP | R1 bindings: staff `.10.21-.23`, student `.20.21-.23`, guest `.30.21`, sensors `.40.21-.23` | Pass |
190: | 802.1X | staff1 on SW2 `Gi0/1` -> VLAN 10; student1 on `Gi1/0` -> VLAN 20; guest1 on SW3 `Gi0/1` -> VLAN 30; `test aaa group CAMPUS-RADIUS` succeeds; RADIUS logs 13 auth responses | Pass |
191: | IoT access | IOSvL2 MAB does not work (see limitations); port security with the fixed sensor MACs authorises the three sensors in VLAN 40 | Pass (design adapted) |
192: | MQTT | `mosquitto_sub -t 'campus/iot/#'` received JSON from `temp-01`, `motion-01`, `humidity-01` | Pass |
193: | ACLs | T11 staff all pass; T12/T13 student/guest Internet HTTP 401 and all RFC1918 pings blocked; T14 IoT MQTT `nc` succeeds, Internet/internal pings blocked; deny counters on all four restricted ACLs | Pass |
194: | NAT | `show ip nat translations` shows staff ICMP and student/guest TCP translated to 10.0.0.1; NAT statistics 18 active, 0 for IoT | Pass |
195: | STP | SW1 root for VLANs 1,10,20,30,40,99; rapid-pvst; no blocking ports | Pass |
196: 
197: Evidence files: `report/evidence/T01-T20-r1.txt`, `T02-T03-T19-sw1.txt`,
198: `T02-T19-sw2.txt`, `T02-T19-sw3.txt`, `T05-T15-sw2-sessions.txt`,
199: `T06-T07-sw3-sessions.txt`, `T09-wrongpass.txt`, `T10-server-dead.txt`,
200: `T11`-`T14` matrices, `T16-mqtt-subscribe.txt`, `T17-T18-r1-acl-nat.txt`,
201: `T18-nat-live.txt`.
202: 
203: **Not demonstrated live:** T08 (moving staff1 to another port). The optional
204: reload in T20 was not performed; T19 is covered by the summary output rather
205: than per-VLAN detail. T10 is proven with `authentication event server dead`
206: (`RADIUS_DEAD` -> VLAN 30 -> DHCP in 192.168.30.0/24); `no-response` is the
207: supplicant-silent event, not the RADIUS-outage event.
208: 
209: ## Offline validation performed
210: 
211: These checks were run in the build environment and do not require GNS3. The
212: Docker daemon socket was not accessible to the build user, so the container
213: checks used rootless **Podman with the same images and mounts**; the Compose
214: file was parsed with Docker Compose v5.6.1. Docker users can run the same
215: commands with `docker` in place of `podman`.
216: 
217: | Check | Command | Result |
218: |---|---|---|
219: | Config consistency | `python3 tests/verify_configs.py` | **415 passed, 0 failed** |
220: | Compose syntax | `docker compose -f radius/docker-compose.yml config` | Valid; network `campus-network_server`, macvlan parent `srv-mac`, RADIUS .10, MQTT .20 |
221: | Server bridge script | `unshare -rn ./radius/setup-server-bridge.sh` in a throwaway network namespace | Creates `br-srv`, `srv-mac` and `srv-br`; `srv-br` is enslaved to `br-srv` |
222: | FreeRADIUS syntax | `freeradius -CX` in `freeradius/freeradius-server:3.2.3` with the repo's `clients.conf` + `users` | **Configuration appears to be OK** |
223: | RADIUS PAP/VLAN | `radtest staff1 ...` and `radtest 0200.0000.4001 ...` | Access-Accept with `Tunnel-Type=VLAN`, `Tunnel-Medium-Type=IEEE-802`, `Tunnel-Private-Group-Id="10"` / `"40"` |
224: | RADIUS MAB aliases | `radtest` with plain, hyphen and colon MAC forms | Access-Accept for all three formats, VLAN 40 |
225: | RADIUS EAP-MD5 | `eapol_test` against the exact supplicant profiles (control-interface line removed for the host test) | **SUCCESS** for staff1/2/3, student1/2/3, guest1; wrong-password profile returns **FAILURE** |
226: | MQTT payload | Local Mosquitto 2.1 + `sensor.py`, three types, 1-second test interval | JSON with `id`, `type`, `value`, `timestamp`; all three IDs observed |
227: | Sensor image | `podman build -t campus-sensor:1.0 endpoints/sensor` | Builds; container publishes to Mosquitto |
228: | Client image | `podman build -t campus-client:1.0 endpoints/client` | Builds; stays running and emits supplicant/DHCP diagnostics |
229: 
230: **Not verified offline:** GNS3 GUI, Cisco IOSv/IOSvL2 command acceptance, real
231: EAPOL on an IOSvL2 switch, end-to-end dynamic VLAN assignment, GNS3 Cloud
232: plumbing, and the complete ACL matrix. Those require the images and GNS3 and
233: are covered by `tests/test-plan.md`.
234: 
235: One implementation correction came out of the offline tests: `wpa_supplicant`
236: 2.10 has no `-f` option, so the client entrypoint redirects stdout/stderr to
237: `/tmp/wpa_supplicant.log` instead. The image was rebuilt and rechecked after
238: that change.
239: 
240: ## Known limitations
241: 
242: - **MAB does not work on IOSvL2.** The image accepts `mab`, `authentication
243:   order mab` and `dot1x pae authenticator`, and the sensor frames reach the
244:   switch port, but no authentication session is ever created and the port
245:   stays unauthorized. This is a known IOSvL2 limitation, not a RADIUS problem:
246:   `radtest` with `0200.0000.4001` returns Access-Accept VLAN 40. The shipped
247:   `SW3.cfg` therefore uses `switchport port-security` with one pinned MAC per
248:   sensor (`violation restrict`); `configs/SW3.cfg` documents the four lines to
249:   swap back on Catalyst hardware. On real hardware MAB would authenticate the
250:   same three MACs against the same `radius/users` entries.
251: - **802.1X is still image-dependent.** If a different IOSvL2 build rejects the
252:   `authentication`/`dot1x` commands, do not invent replacement syntax; use the
253:   same port-security fallback and state the limitation in the report.
254: - **Packet Tracer cannot do this part.** Use GNS3 or EVE-NG.
255: - **The simulated Internet has no DNS or HTTPS service.** R2 answers ICMP and
256:   HTTP on 8.8.8.8. DNS and HTTPS tests prove the ACL permits via counters, not
257:   a successful application response. Add a DNS/HTTPS container to the server
258:   segment if the report needs those responses.
259: - **EAP-MD5 is lab-only.** It is not a production authentication method.
260: - **Anonymous MQTT.** The broker is intentionally open on the isolated IoT
261:   VLAN; add authentication/TLS for anything real.
262: - **The Docker server segment is host-dependent.** The macvlan/veth/bridge
263:   setup must exist on the GNS3 server host. A GNS3 VM needs the same setup
264:   inside the VM. The Cloud node must select `br-srv`.
265: - **Unclean host shutdowns lose running configs.** The QEMU overlays use
266:   write-back caching, so a hard power-off or crash can drop what `write
267:   memory` wrote; a clean `stop`/`start` of a node keeps it (verified on SW3).
268:   After an unclean reboot, re-paste `configs/*.cfg`, `write memory`, and
269:   restart the Cloud node so it re-attaches to `br-srv`. Recreating the bridge
270:   and veth pair needs root: `radius/setup-server-bridge.sh`.
271: - **Docker endpoint capabilities.** The client and sensor containers need
272:   `NET_ADMIN` (and `NET_RAW` for `wpa_supplicant -D wired`) to send EAPOL and,
273:   for sensors, to override the MAC. GNS3 normally grants these to Docker
274:   nodes; if your install does not, run the endpoint containers privileged or
275:   set the sensor MAC in the GNS3 node properties.
276: - **MAC format for MAB.** Cisco IOS normally sends `0200.0000.4001`. The
277:   `radius/users` file includes aliases for dotted, plain, hyphen and colon
278:   forms. If your image sends some other format (for example uppercase),
279:   `radiusd -X` shows the exact User-Name; add one alias with that string.
280: - **No high availability.** SW1 is a single distribution switch and R1 is a
281:   single gateway; this matches the brief but is not resilient.
282: 
283: ## Troubleshooting quick reference
284: 
285: | Problem | Check | Fix |
286: |---|---|---|
287: | `verify_configs.py` fails | The message names the file/field | Fix the generated file, rerun |
288: | Compose cannot create the macvlan network | `ip link show srv-mac` | Run `radius/setup-server-bridge.sh`; ensure the parent is up |
289: | `br-srv` missing in GNS3 Cloud | GNS3 server host / VM | Run the setup script on the GNS3 server host; restart the GNS3 server |
290: | RADIUS container exits | `docker logs radius` | Validate config with `freeradius -CX`; check mounts |
291: | Switch cannot ping 192.168.50.10 | SW SVI, VLAN 99 trunk, R1 `MGMT_IN` counters | `show ip interface brief`; `show interfaces trunk`; `show access-lists` |
292: | `mab` configured but no session | IOSvL2 MAB is non-functional | Use port security; see the note in `configs/SW3.cfg` |
293: | Client gets no DHCP | `show authentication sessions`, `show dot1x all` | Confirm EAP success/fallback; `docker exec ... cat /tmp/wpa_supplicant.log` |
294: | Client authenticated in wrong VLAN | RADIUS debug Tunnel-Private-Group-Id | Check the `users` entry and `aaa authorization network default group CAMPUS-RADIUS` |
295: | Sensor not authorized | MAC differs from the port-security entry | `show port-security interface Gi0/2`; set the GNS3 MAC or `SENSOR_MAC` |
296: | MQTT no messages | Sensor DHCP, IOT_IN 1883 permit, broker | `docker logs <sensor>`; `show access-lists`; `docker exec mqtt mosquitto_sub ...` |
297: | Trunk not forwarding VLAN | `show interfaces trunk` allowed list | Repaste the trunk block; check both ends |
298: 
299: ## What to read next
300: 
301: - Build: [topology/gns3-build-steps.md](topology/gns3-build-steps.md)
302: - Design tables: [topology/topology.md](topology/topology.md)
303: - Tests: [tests/test-plan.md](tests/test-plan.md)
304: - Report structure: [report/report-outline.md](report/report-outline.md)
305: - RADIUS details: [radius/users](radius/users), [radius/clients.conf](radius/clients.conf)

(End of file - total 305 lines)

# Segmented Campus Network - GNS3 Build Kit

A complete, paste-ready GNS3 lab for:

- **2 routers** (R1 campus gateway/firewall/DHCP/NAT, R2 simulated ISP)
- **3 switches** (SW1 distribution, SW2 staff/student access, SW3 guest/IoT access)
- **STAFF VLAN** with 3 Docker clients
- **STUDENT VLAN** with 3 Docker clients
- **GUEST VLAN** with 1 Docker client
- **IOT VLAN** with 3 real Docker sensors publishing MQTT
- **Firewall policy** as five named extended ACLs on R1
- **RADIUS dynamic VLAN** using FreeRADIUS and 802.1X for users (MAB-ready
  RADIUS entries for sensors)
- **MQTT broker** and a server segment isolated behind R1

The lab was built and run end to end in GNS3 3.1 with IOSv/IOSvL2 images:
802.1X dynamic VLAN assignment, DHCP, MQTT, the ACL matrices and NAT were
exercised and the captured output is in `report/evidence/`. See
[Live validation performed](#live-validation-performed-gns3-31-iosviiosvl2)
for the results and the one platform gap (MAB on IOSvL2).

## What you must supply

1. **Cisco IOSv image** for R1 and R2 (IOS 15.x, at least 3 GigabitEthernet
   interfaces). Import it into GNS3 as an IOSv QEMU template.
2. **Cisco IOSvL2 image** for SW1, SW2, SW3 (IOS 15.2-class, at least 8
   GigabitEthernet interfaces, 802.1X-capable feature set). Import it as an
   IOSvL2 QEMU template and mark it as an Ethernet switch.
3. **GNS3 2.2.x** with a local Linux server (or a GNS3 VM with Docker).
4. **Docker Engine + Compose v2** on the GNS3 server host, for FreeRADIUS,
   Mosquitto and the endpoint images.

The Cisco images are **not** included and cannot be redistributed here. No
image filenames are assumed: use whatever IOSv/IOSvL2 images you are licensed
to use, then match the interface names in the configs.

You do **not** need Packet Tracer. Packet Tracer cannot do this lab's RADIUS
dynamic VLAN and MAB behavior; use GNS3 or EVE-NG.

## Repository layout

```
network-project/
  README.md                       this file
  topology/
    topology.md                   diagram, port map, addressing
    gns3-build-steps.md           click-by-click GNS3 build and paste order
  configs/
    R1.cfg R2.cfg                 routers
    SW1.cfg SW2.cfg SW3.cfg       switches
  radius/
    docker-compose.yml            FreeRADIUS + Mosquitto on the server segment
    clients.conf                  SW1/SW2/SW3 RADIUS clients + secret
    users                         users, MAC users, Tunnel-* VLAN attributes
    secrets.env                   canonical list of lab secrets/placeholders
    mosquitto.conf                lab broker (anonymous, port 1883)
    setup-server-bridge.sh        br-srv + veth + macvlan plumbing
  endpoints/

## First 10 minutes

Run these in order. Stop and fix any error before building the GNS3 topology.

### 1. Check the generated files

```sh
cd network-project
python3 tests/verify_configs.py
```

Expected last line: `SUMMARY: ... 0 failed`.

### 2. Prepare the Docker server segment

```sh
cd radius
chmod +x setup-server-bridge.sh
./setup-server-bridge.sh
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
docker logs radius --tail 30
```

Wait for `Ready to process requests` in the FreeRADIUS log. The script creates
`br-srv` and the `srv-mac`/`srv-br` veth pair. The GNS3 Cloud node attaches to
`br-srv`; R1 g0/1 connects to that Cloud. R1 is `192.168.50.1` and is the
containers' default gateway.

If GNS3 runs inside a **GNS3 VM**, do this inside the VM and attach the Cloud
node to the VM's `br-srv`. A local GNS3 server on the same Linux host is the
simplest setup. Do not run Compose on your desktop while GNS3 runs in a VM that
cannot see that bridge.

### 3. Build endpoint images

```sh
cd ..            # back to network-project/
docker build -t campus-client:1.0 endpoints/client
docker build -t campus-sensor:1.0 endpoints/sensor
```

### 4. Build the GNS3 project

Follow [topology/gns3-build-steps.md](topology/gns3-build-steps.md). It has the
node list, 15 links, Docker environment variables, startup order and the exact
paste procedure.

Recommended startup order: **RADIUS/MQTT -> SW1/SW2/SW3 -> R1/R2 -> endpoints**.

Recommended config paste order: **SW1 -> SW2 -> SW3 -> R1 -> R2**, ending each
with `end` and `write memory`.

### 5. Run the tests

Use [tests/test-plan.md](tests/test-plan.md). The minimum evidence set is in
[report/report-outline.md](report/report-outline.md#screenshot-checklist-minimum).

## Secrets and consistency

`radius/secrets.env` is the canonical list, but Cisco IOS and FreeRADIUS cannot
read it directly, so values are repeated in the files they configure. Before
using the lab outside an isolated GNS3 project, change:

| Secret | Where it appears |
|---|---|
| `RADIUS_SECRET` | `radius/secrets.env`, `radius/clients.conf` (4 clients), `configs/SW1.cfg`, `SW2.cfg`, `SW3.cfg` (`key 0 ...`) |
| `DEVICE_ENABLE_SECRET` | `radius/secrets.env`, `enable secret` and `username admin ... secret` in all five Cisco configs |
| Staff/student/guest passwords | `radius/secrets.env`, `radius/users`, `endpoints/client/wpa_supplicant-*.conf` |
| Sensor MACs | `radius/secrets.env`, `radius/users`, GNS3 Docker node MAC / `SENSOR_MAC` |

The checked-in value `S3cr3t-Shared-Key-2026` is a **placeholder shared
secret**; it is intentionally easy to find. `tests/verify_configs.py` checks
that the copies stay in sync but does not judge their strength.

Do not commit real production secrets. Do not expose the lab's anonymous MQTT
broker or RADIUS shared secret outside the isolated lab network.

## RADIUS authentication choice

Users authenticate with **EAP-MD5**. The stock FreeRADIUS 3.2 image enables
`default_eap_type = md5` and needs no client certificate, so the lab is
reproducible without a PKI. `wpa_supplicant` is started with the wired driver:
`wpa_supplicant -i eth0 -D wired -c <profile>`. The sensor and client
entrypoints request DHCP after authentication.

For PEAP/MSCHAPv2 or EAP-TLS, add a CA/server certificate, set `eap=PEAP` and
`phase2="auth=MSCHAPV2"` (or `eap=TLS`) in the supplicant profiles, and update
the FreeRADIUS `eap` module. EAP-MD5 is deprecated for production Wi-Fi but is
appropriate for this wired lab.

## Known limitations

- **MAB does not work on IOSvL2.** The image accepts `mab`, `authentication
  order mab` and `dot1x pae authenticator`, and the sensor frames reach the
  switch port, but no authentication session is ever created and the port
  stays unauthorized. This is a known IOSvL2 limitation, not a RADIUS problem:
  `radtest` with `0200.0000.4001` returns Access-Accept VLAN 40. The shipped
  `SW3.cfg` therefore uses `switchport port-security` with one pinned MAC per
  sensor (`violation restrict`); `configs/SW3.cfg` documents the four lines to
  swap back on Catalyst hardware. On real hardware MAB would authenticate the
  same three MACs against the same `radius/users` entries.
- **802.1X is still image-dependent.** If a different IOSvL2 build rejects the
  `authentication`/`dot1x` commands, do not invent replacement syntax; use the
  same port-security fallback and state the limitation in the report.
- **Packet Tracer cannot do this part.** Use GNS3 or EVE-NG.
- **The simulated Internet has no DNS or HTTPS service.** R2 answers ICMP and
  HTTP on 8.8.8.8. DNS and HTTPS tests prove the ACL permits via counters, not
  a successful application response. Add a DNS/HTTPS container to the server
  segment if the report needs those responses.
- **EAP-MD5 is lab-only.** It is not a production authentication method.
- **Anonymous MQTT.** The broker is intentionally open on the isolated IoT
  VLAN; add authentication/TLS for anything real.
- **The Docker server segment is host-dependent.** The macvlan/veth/bridge
  setup must exist on the GNS3 server host. A GNS3 VM needs the same setup
  inside the VM. The Cloud node must select `br-srv`.
- **Unclean host shutdowns lose running configs.** The QEMU overlays use
  write-back caching, so a hard power-off or crash can drop what `write
  memory` wrote; a clean `stop`/`start` of a node keeps it (verified on SW3).
  After an unclean reboot, re-paste `configs/*.cfg`, `write memory`, and
  restart the Cloud node so it re-attaches to `br-srv`. Recreating the bridge
  and veth pair needs root: `radius/setup-server-bridge.sh`.
- **Docker endpoint capabilities.** The client and sensor containers need
  `NET_ADMIN` (and `NET_RAW` for `wpa_supplicant -D wired`) to send EAPOL and,
  for sensors, to override the MAC. GNS3 normally grants these to Docker
  nodes; if your install does not, run the endpoint containers privileged or
  set the sensor MAC in the GNS3 node properties.
- **MAC format for MAB.** Cisco IOS normally sends `0200.0000.4001`. The
  `radius/users` file includes aliases for dotted, plain, hyphen and colon
  forms. If your image sends some other format (for example uppercase),
  `radiusd -X` shows the exact User-Name; add one alias with that string.
- **No high availability.** SW1 is a single distribution switch and R1 is a
  single gateway; this matches the brief but is not resilient.

## Troubleshooting quick reference

| Problem | Check | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `verify_configs.py` fails | The message names the file/field | Fix the generated file, rerun |
| Compose cannot create the macvlan network | `ip link show srv-mac` | Run `radius/setup-server-bridge.sh`; ensure the parent is up |
| `br-srv` missing in GNS3 Cloud | GNS3 server host / VM | Run the setup script on the GNS3 server host; restart the GNS3 server |
| RADIUS container exits | `docker logs radius` | Validate config with `freeradius -CX`; check mounts |
| Switch cannot ping 192.168.50.10 | SW SVI, VLAN 99 trunk, R1 `MGMT_IN` counters | `show ip interface brief`; `show interfaces trunk`; `show access-lists` |
| `mab` configured but no session | IOSvL2 MAB is non-functional | Use port security; see the note in `configs/SW3.cfg` |
| Client gets no DHCP | `show authentication sessions`, `show dot1x all` | Confirm EAP success/fallback; `docker exec ... cat /tmp/wpa_supplicant.log` |
| Client authenticated in wrong VLAN | RADIUS debug Tunnel-Private-Group-Id | Check the `users` entry and `aaa authorization network default group CAMPUS-RADIUS` |
| Sensor not authorized | MAC differs from the port-security entry | `show port-security interface Gi0/2`; set the GNS3 MAC or `SENSOR_MAC` |
| MQTT no messages | Sensor DHCP, IOT_IN 1883 permit, broker | `docker logs <sensor>`; `show access-lists`; `docker exec mqtt mosquitto_sub ...` |
| Trunk not forwarding VLAN | `show interfaces trunk` allowed list | Repaste the trunk block; check both ends |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline consistency checks for the segmented campus network project.

This does NOT validate Cisco IOS syntax on a real image. It checks that the
generated artefacts agree with the design in topology/topology.md and with each
other: addressing, VLANs, trunks, access ports, ACLs, DHCP, NAT, RADIUS users,
client supplicant profiles and the Docker server segment.

Run:
    python3 tests/verify_configs.py
Exit code 0 = all checks passed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ipaddress
import re
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CONFIGS = ROOT / "configs"
RADIUS = ROOT / "radius"
CLIENTS = ROOT / "endpoints" / "client"
SENSOR = ROOT / "endpoints" / "sensor"

SWITCHES = ("SW1", "SW2", "SW3")
EXPECTED_VLANS = {10: "STAFF", 20: "STUDENT", 30: "GUEST", 40: "IOT", 99: "MGMT"}
TRUNK_VLANS = {10, 20, 30, 40, 99}
EXPECTED_TRUNKS = {
    "SW1": {"GigabitEthernet0/0", "GigabitEthernet0/1", "GigabitEthernet0/2"},
    "SW2": {"GigabitEthernet0/0"},
    "SW3": {"GigabitEthernet0/0"},
}
# (switch, port) -> (access VLAN, node name in description)
EXPECTED_ACCESS = {
    ("SW2", "GigabitEthernet0/1"): (10, "STAFF-PC1"),
    ("SW2", "GigabitEthernet0/2"): (10, "STAFF-PC2"),
    ("SW2", "GigabitEthernet0/3"): (10, "STAFF-PC3"),
    ("SW2", "GigabitEthernet1/0"): (20, "STUDENT-PC1"),
    ("SW2", "GigabitEthernet1/1"): (20, "STUDENT-PC2"),
    ("SW2", "GigabitEthernet1/2"): (20, "STUDENT-PC3"),
    ("SW3", "GigabitEthernet0/1"): (30, "GUEST-PC1"),
    ("SW3", "GigabitEthernet0/2"): (40, "SENSOR-TEMP"),
    ("SW3", "GigabitEthernet0/3"): (40, "SENSOR-MOTION"),
    ("SW3", "GigabitEthernet1/0"): (40, "SENSOR-HUMIDITY"),
}
MGMT_IPS = {"SW1": "192.168.99.11", "SW2": "192.168.99.12", "SW3": "192.168.99.13"}
SENSOR_PORTS = {
    "GigabitEthernet0/2": "0200.0000.4001",
    "GigabitEthernet0/3": "0200.0000.4002",
    "GigabitEthernet1/0": "0200.0000.4003",
}
EXPECTED_ACLS = {"STAFF_IN", "STUDENT_IN", "GUEST_IN", "IOT_IN", "MGMT_IN"}

EXPECTED_USERS = {
    "staff1": ("10", "Staff1Pass!"),
    "staff2": ("10", "Staff2Pass!"),
    "staff3": ("10", "Staff3Pass!"),
    "student1": ("20", "Student1Pass!"),
    "student2": ("20", "Student2Pass!"),
    "student3": ("20", "Student3Pass!"),
    "guest1": ("30", "Guest1Pass!"),
    "0200.0000.4001": ("40", None),
    "0200.0000.4002": ("40", None),
    "0200.0000.4003": ("40", None),
}
SENSOR_MAC_ENV = {
    "SENSOR_MAC_TEMP": "0200.0000.4001",
    "SENSOR_MAC_MOTION": "0200.0000.4002",
    "SENSOR_MAC_HUMIDITY": "0200.0000.4003",
}


class Checker:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.passed = 0
        self.failed: list[str] = []

    def check(self, condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
        if condition:
            self.passed += 1
            print(f"[PASS] {message}")
        else:
            self.failed.append(message)
            print(f"[FAIL] {message}")

    def contains(self, haystack: str, needle: str, message: str) -> None:
        self.check(needle in haystack, message)

    def summary(self) -> int:
        print()
        print("=" * 72)
        print(f"SUMMARY: {self.passed} passed, {len(self.failed)} failed")
        if self.failed:
            print()
            for item in self.failed:
                print(f"  - {item}")
            return 1
        return 0


def read(path: Path) -> str:
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing required file: {path}")
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def parse_blocks(text: str, header_re: re.Pattern[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """Parse IOS-style indented blocks, e.g. interface or ACL stanzas."""
    blocks: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    current: str | None = None
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        if not raw.strip():
            continue
        if raw[0].isspace():
            if current is not None:
                blocks[current].append(raw.strip())
            continue
        match = header_re.match(raw)
        if match:
            current = match.group(1)
            blocks[current] = []
            continue
        # Any top-level line, including '!', closes the current block.
        current = None
    return blocks


def block_text(blocks: dict[str, list[str]], name: str) -> str:
    return "\n".join(blocks.get(name, []))


def parse_vlan_list(value: str) -> set[int]:
    result: set[int] = set()
    for part in value.split(","):
        part = part.strip()
        if not part:
            continue
        if "-" in part:
            start, end = part.split("-", 1)
            result.update(range(int(start), int(end) + 1))
        else:
            result.add(int(part))
    return result


def parse_env(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    env: dict[str, str] = {}
    for raw in read(path).splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, value = line.split("=", 1)
        env[key.strip()] = value.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    return env


def parse_users(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return username -> joined attribute text for a FreeRADIUS users file."""
    entries: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    current: str | None = None
    for raw in read(path).splitlines():
        if not raw.strip() or raw.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        if raw[0].isspace():
            if current is not None:
                entries[current].append(raw.strip())
            continue
        parts = raw.split(None, 1)
        current = parts[0]
        entries[current] = [parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else ""]
    return {name: " ".join(parts) for name, parts in entries.items()}


def main() -> int:
    c = Checker()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Required delivery files
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    required = [
        ROOT / "README.md",
        ROOT / "topology" / "topology.md",
        ROOT / "topology" / "gns3-build-steps.md",
        ROOT / "tests" / "test-plan.md",
        ROOT / "report" / "report-outline.md",
        RADIUS / "docker-compose.yml",
        RADIUS / "clients.conf",
        RADIUS / "users",
        RADIUS / "secrets.env",
        RADIUS / "mosquitto.conf",
        RADIUS / "setup-server-bridge.sh",
        SENSOR / "Dockerfile",
        SENSOR / "sensor.py",
        CLIENTS / "Dockerfile",
        CLIENTS / "entrypoint.sh",
    ]
    for path in required:
        c.check(path.exists(), f"required file exists: {path.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    for name in ("R1", "R2", "SW1", "SW2", "SW3"):
        c.check((CONFIGS / f"{name}.cfg").exists(), f"required config exists: configs/{name}.cfg")

    if c.failed:
        # Avoid a cascade of confusing parse errors when files are missing.
        return c.summary()

    cfg = {name: read(CONFIGS / f"{name}.cfg") for name in ("R1", "R2", "SW1", "SW2", "SW3")}
    clients_conf = read(RADIUS / "clients.conf")
    users = parse_users(RADIUS / "users")
    env = parse_env(RADIUS / "secrets.env")
    compose = read(RADIUS / "docker-compose.yml")
    mosquitto = read(RADIUS / "mosquitto.conf")
    topology = read(ROOT / "topology" / "topology.md")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Basic structure and hostnames
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for name, text in cfg.items():
        c.check(re.search(rf"^hostname {name}$", text, re.M) is not None, f"{name}: hostname is {name}")
        c.check(text.rstrip().endswith("end"), f"{name}: config ends with 'end'")
        c.check("enable secret " in text, f"{name}: enable secret configured")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # VLAN database on every switch
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    switch_ifaces: dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]] = {}
    switch_vlans: dict[str, dict[int, str]] = {}
    for sw in SWITCHES:
        text = cfg[sw]
        switch_ifaces[sw] = parse_blocks(text, re.compile(r"^interface\s+(\S+)$"))
        vlan_blocks = parse_blocks(text, re.compile(r"^vlan\s+(\d+)$"))
        found: dict[int, str] = {}
        for vid, lines in vlan_blocks.items():
            match = re.search(r"^name\s+(\S+)$", "\n".join(lines), re.M)
            found[int(vid)] = match.group(1) if match else ""
        switch_vlans[sw] = found
        for vid, name in EXPECTED_VLANS.items():
            c.check(found.get(vid) == name, f"{sw}: VLAN {vid} exists and is named {name}")
        c.check("spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst" in text, f"{sw}: rapid-pvst enabled")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Trunks and access ports
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    configured_trunks: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    configured_access: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = {}
    for sw in SWITCHES:
        trunks: set[str] = set()
        for iface, lines in switch_ifaces[sw].items():
            block = "\n".join(lines)
            if re.search(r"^switchport mode trunk$", block, re.M):
                trunks.add(iface)
                allowed_match = re.search(r"^switchport trunk allowed vlan (.+)$", block, re.M)
                c.check(allowed_match is not None, f"{sw} {iface}: trunk has explicit allowed VLAN list")
                if allowed_match:
                    allowed = parse_vlan_list(allowed_match.group(1))
                    c.check(
                        allowed == TRUNK_VLANS,
                        f"{sw} {iface}: trunk allowed VLANs are exactly {sorted(TRUNK_VLANS)}",
                    )
            access_match = re.search(r"^switchport access vlan (\d+)$", block, re.M)
            if access_match:
                configured_access[(sw, iface)] = int(access_match.group(1))
        configured_trunks[sw] = trunks
        c.check(
            trunks == EXPECTED_TRUNKS[sw],
            f"{sw}: trunk ports are exactly {sorted(EXPECTED_TRUNKS[sw])}",
        )

    c.check(
        set(configured_access) == set(EXPECTED_ACCESS),
        "access-port map has exactly the expected ports and no extra access ports",
    )

    for (sw, iface), (vlan, node) in EXPECTED_ACCESS.items():
        lines = switch_ifaces[sw].get(iface, [])
        block = "\n".join(lines)
        c.check(bool(lines), f"{sw} {iface}: interface is configured")
        c.check(
            configured_access.get((sw, iface)) == vlan,
            f"{sw} {iface}: access VLAN is {vlan}",
        )
        c.check(
            re.search(r"^switchport mode access$", block, re.M) is not None,
            f"{sw} {iface}: switchport mode access",
        )
        c.check(node in block, f"{sw} {iface}: description identifies {node}")
        if vlan in (10, 20, 30):
            c.check(
                re.search(r"^authentication port-control auto$", block, re.M) is not None,
                f"{sw} {iface}: authentication port-control auto",
            )
            c.check(
                re.search(r"^dot1x pae authenticator$", block, re.M) is not None,
                f"{sw} {iface}: dot1x pae authenticator",
            )
            c.check(
                re.search(r"^authentication order dot1x$", block, re.M) is not None,
                f"{sw} {iface}: 802.1X is first authentication method",
            )
            c.check(
                "authentication event fail action authorize vlan 30" in block,
                f"{sw} {iface}: failed auth falls back to VLAN 30",
            )
            c.check(
                "authentication event server dead action authorize vlan 30" in block,
                f"{sw} {iface}: dead RADIUS server falls back to VLAN 30",
            )
            c.check(
                "authentication event no-response action authorize vlan 30" in block,
                f"{sw} {iface}: supplicant no-response falls back to VLAN 30",
            )
            c.check(
                "mab" not in [line.strip() for line in lines],
                f"{sw} {iface}: user port is not MAB-only",
            )
        else:
            # IOSvL2 accepts "mab" but never creates an authentication session,
            # so the shipped configs pin the sensor MAC with port security.
            sensor_mac = SENSOR_PORTS.get(iface)
            c.check(
                sensor_mac is not None and f"switchport port-security mac-address {sensor_mac}" in block,
                f"{sw} {iface}: port security pins sensor MAC {sensor_mac}",
            )
            c.check(
                re.search(r"^switchport port-security maximum 1$", block, re.M) is not None,
                f"{sw} {iface}: port security allows one MAC",
            )
            c.check(
                re.search(r"^switchport port-security violation restrict$", block, re.M) is not None,
                f"{sw} {iface}: port security restricts unknown MACs",
            )
            c.check(
                "authentication event fail action authorize vlan 30" not in block,
                f"{sw} {iface}: failed IoT auth is not moved to guest VLAN",
            )

    # Spanning tree root only on SW1.
    c.check(
        "spanning-tree vlan 10,20,30,40,99 root primary" in cfg["SW1"],
        "SW1: spanning-tree root primary for all VLANs",
    )
    for sw in ("SW2", "SW3"):
        c.check("root primary" not in cfg[sw], f"{sw}: does not claim spanning-tree root")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Management SVIs and default gateways
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for sw, ip in MGMT_IPS.items():
        block = block_text(switch_ifaces[sw], "Vlan99")
        c.check(re.search(rf"^ip address {re.escape(ip)} 255\.255\.255\.0$", block, re.M) is not None,
                f"{sw}: Vlan99 address is {ip}")
        c.check("ip default-gateway 192.168.99.1" in cfg[sw], f"{sw}: default gateway is 192.168.99.1")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # R1 addressing, subinterfaces, ACL application, NAT, DHCP
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    r1_ifaces = parse_blocks(cfg["R1"], re.compile(r"^interface\s+(\S+)$"))
    expected_r1 = {
        "GigabitEthernet0/0.10": ("192.168.10.1", "255.255.255.0", 10, "STAFF_IN"),
        "GigabitEthernet0/0.20": ("192.168.20.1", "255.255.255.0", 20, "STUDENT_IN"),
        "GigabitEthernet0/0.30": ("192.168.30.1", "255.255.255.0", 30, "GUEST_IN"),
        "GigabitEthernet0/0.40": ("192.168.40.1", "255.255.255.0", 40, "IOT_IN"),
        "GigabitEthernet0/0.99": ("192.168.99.1", "255.255.255.0", 99, "MGMT_IN"),
        "GigabitEthernet0/1": ("192.168.50.1", "255.255.255.0", None, None),
        "GigabitEthernet0/2": ("10.0.0.1", "255.255.255.252", None, None),
    }
    for iface, (ip, mask, vlan, acl) in expected_r1.items():
        block = block_text(r1_ifaces, iface)
        c.check(
            re.search(rf"^ip address {re.escape(ip)} {re.escape(mask)}$", block, re.M) is not None,
            f"R1 {iface}: address is {ip}/{mask}",
        )
        if vlan is not None:
            c.check(
                re.search(rf"^encapsulation dot1Q {vlan}$", block, re.M) is not None,
                f"R1 {iface}: encapsulation dot1Q {vlan}",
            )
            c.check(
                re.search(rf"^ip access-group {acl} in$", block, re.M) is not None,
                f"R1 {iface}: {acl} applied inbound",
            )
        if vlan in (10, 20, 30, 40):
            c.check("ip nat inside" in block, f"R1 {iface}: NAT inside")
        if iface == "GigabitEthernet0/2":
            c.check("ip nat outside" in block, f"R1 {iface}: NAT outside")
        if iface == "GigabitEthernet0/1":
            c.check("ip nat inside" not in block, "R1 server interface is not NATed")

    c.check("ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 10.0.0.2" in cfg["R1"], "R1: default route via R2")
    c.check(
        "ip nat inside source list NAT_INSIDE interface GigabitEthernet0/2 overload" in cfg["R1"],
        "R1: PAT overload on the R2 link",
    )
    nat_block = block_text(parse_blocks(cfg["R1"], re.compile(r"^ip access-list standard (\S+)$")), "NAT_INSIDE")
    for vlan in (10, 20, 30, 40):
        c.check(
            f"permit 192.168.{vlan}.0 0.0.0.255" in nat_block,
            f"R1: NAT ACL includes VLAN {vlan} subnet",
        )
    c.check("permit 192.168.50.0 0.0.0.255" not in nat_block, "R1: server subnet is not NATed")
    c.check("permit 192.168.99.0 0.0.0.255" not in nat_block, "R1: MGMT subnet is not NATed")

    for vlan in (10, 20, 30, 40):
        c.check(
            f"ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.{vlan}.1 192.168.{vlan}.20" in cfg["R1"],
            f"R1: DHCP excludes .1-.20 for VLAN {vlan}",
        )
        c.check(
            f"network 192.168.{vlan}.0 255.255.255.0" in cfg["R1"],
            f"R1: DHCP pool exists for VLAN {vlan}",
        )
        c.check(
            f"default-router 192.168.{vlan}.1" in cfg["R1"],
            f"R1: DHCP default router for VLAN {vlan}",
        )
    c.check("service dhcp" in cfg["R1"], "R1: DHCP service enabled")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # ACL definitions and references
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    acl_blocks = parse_blocks(cfg["R1"], re.compile(r"^ip access-list extended (\S+)$"))
    defined_acls = set(acl_blocks)
    c.check(defined_acls == EXPECTED_ACLS, "R1: exactly the five required named extended ACLs exist")
    for acl, lines in acl_blocks.items():
        meaningful = [line for line in lines if line and not line.startswith("remark")]
        c.check(
            meaningful and meaningful[-1] == "deny ip any any log",
            f"R1: ACL {acl} ends with 'deny ip any any log'",
        )
    c.check("permit ip any any" in acl_blocks.get("STAFF_IN", []), "R1: STAFF_IN permits all traffic")
    for acl in ("STUDENT_IN", "GUEST_IN", "IOT_IN", "MGMT_IN"):
        c.check(
            "permit ip any any" not in acl_blocks.get(acl, []),
            f"R1: ACL {acl} does not contain a blanket permit",
        )
    c.check(
        any("deny ip any 192.168.0.0 0.0.255.255" == line for line in acl_blocks.get("STUDENT_IN", [])),
        "R1: STUDENT_IN denies all 192.168/16 destinations before Internet permits",
    )
    c.check(
        any("deny ip any 192.168.0.0 0.0.255.255" == line for line in acl_blocks.get("GUEST_IN", [])),
        "R1: GUEST_IN denies all 192.168/16 destinations",
    )
    for acl in ("STUDENT_IN", "GUEST_IN"):
        joined = "\n".join(acl_blocks.get(acl, []))
        for needle, label in (
            ("permit udp any any eq domain", "DNS/UDP"),
            ("permit tcp any any eq domain", "DNS/TCP"),
            ("permit tcp any any eq www", "HTTP"),
            ("permit tcp any any eq 443", "HTTPS"),
            ("permit tcp any any established", "established return traffic"),
        ):
            c.check(needle in joined, f"R1: {acl} permits {label}")
    iot_joined = "\n".join(acl_blocks.get("IOT_IN", []))
    c.check("permit tcp any host 192.168.50.20 eq 1883" in iot_joined, "R1: IOT_IN permits MQTT to .20:1883")
    c.check("permit udp any eq bootpc any eq bootps" in iot_joined, "R1: IOT_IN permits DHCP")
    mgmt_joined = "\n".join(acl_blocks.get("MGMT_IN", []))
    c.check("host 192.168.50.10 eq 1812" in mgmt_joined, "R1: MGMT_IN permits RADIUS auth 1812")
    c.check("host 192.168.50.10 eq 1813" in mgmt_joined, "R1: MGMT_IN permits RADIUS accounting 1813")
    c.check("192.168.99.0 0.0.0.255" in mgmt_joined, "R1: MGMT_IN is scoped to the MGMT subnet")

    # Every ACL referenced in an interface must exist.
    referenced = set()
    for iface, lines in r1_ifaces.items():
        for line in lines:
            match = re.match(r"^ip access-group (\S+) (in|out)$", line)
            if match:
                referenced.add(match.group(1))
    c.check(referenced <= defined_acls, "R1: every referenced ACL is defined")
    c.check(referenced == EXPECTED_ACLS, "R1: all five ACLs are actually applied")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unique IPs and no overlapping subnets
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    ip_owner: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    networks: list[tuple[ipaddress._BaseNetwork, str]] = []  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    for name, text in cfg.items():
        for match in re.finditer(
            r"^\s*ip address (\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{1,3}){3}) (\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{1,3}){3})\s*$",
            text,
            re.M,
        ):
            ip, mask = match.group(1), match.group(2)
            ip_owner[ip].append(name)
            try:
                iface = ipaddress.ip_interface(f"{ip}/{mask}")
                networks.append((iface.network, f"{name}:{ip}"))
            except ValueError:
                c.check(False, f"{name}: invalid IP/mask {ip}/{mask}")
    duplicates = {ip: owners for ip, owners in ip_owner.items() if len(owners) > 1}
    c.check(not duplicates, f"no duplicate IP addresses (found {duplicates or 'none'})")
    overlaps: list[str] = []
    for idx, (net_a, owner_a) in enumerate(networks):
        for net_b, owner_b in networks[idx + 1:]:
            # Multiple interfaces on the same subnet are intentional (VLAN 99,
            # the /30 link). Only a partial overlap is a design error.
            if net_a.overlaps(net_b) and net_a != net_b:
                overlaps.append(f"{owner_a} {net_a} <-> {owner_b} {net_b}")
    c.check(not overlaps, f"no partially overlapping subnets (found {overlaps or 'none'})")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # R2
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    r2_ifaces = parse_blocks(cfg["R2"], re.compile(r"^interface\s+(\S+)$"))
    c.check("ip address 8.8.8.8 255.255.255.255" in block_text(r2_ifaces, "Loopback0"),
            "R2: loopback 8.8.8.8/32")
    c.check("ip address 10.0.0.2 255.255.255.252" in block_text(r2_ifaces, "GigabitEthernet0/0"),
            "R2: link address 10.0.0.2/30")
    c.check("ip route 192.168.0.0 255.255.0.0 10.0.0.1" in cfg["R2"],
            "R2: return route for 192.168.0.0/16")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # RADIUS: switch clients, shared secret, users, reply attributes
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    c.check("ip radius source-interface Vlan99" in cfg["SW1"], "SW1: RADIUS source interface is Vlan99")
    for sw in SWITCHES:
        text = cfg[sw]
        c.check("aaa new-model" in text, f"{sw}: aaa new-model")
        c.check("radius server RADIUS-1" in text, f"{sw}: radius server RADIUS-1")
        c.check("address ipv4 192.168.50.10 auth-port 1812 acct-port 1813" in text,
                f"{sw}: RADIUS server address/ports")
        c.check("aaa group server radius CAMPUS-RADIUS" in text,
                f"{sw}: named RADIUS server group CAMPUS-RADIUS")
        c.check("server name RADIUS-1" in text,
                f"{sw}: RADIUS-1 is a member of the server group")
        c.check("aaa authentication dot1x default group CAMPUS-RADIUS" in text,
                f"{sw}: dot1x authentication uses RADIUS")
        c.check("aaa authorization network default group CAMPUS-RADIUS" in text,
                f"{sw}: network authorization uses RADIUS (needed for dynamic VLAN)")
        c.check("aaa accounting dot1x default start-stop group CAMPUS-RADIUS" in text,
                f"{sw}: dot1x accounting uses RADIUS")
        c.check("dot1x system-auth-control" in text, f"{sw}: dot1x system-auth-control")
        c.check("ip radius source-interface Vlan99" in text, f"{sw}: RADIUS source interface is Vlan99")
        if sw in ("SW2", "SW3"):
            c.check("radius-server dead-criteria time 10 tries 2" in text,
                    f"{sw}: RADIUS dead detection tuned so T10 fallback triggers quickly")

    keys: dict[str, str] = {}
    for sw in SWITCHES:
        match = re.search(r"^\s*key 0 (\S+)$", cfg[sw], re.M)
        c.check(match is not None, f"{sw}: RADIUS key configured")
        if match:

    c.check(len(set(keys.values())) == 1, "all switches use the same RADIUS key")
    secret_env = env.get("RADIUS_SECRET")

    if secret_env:
        c.check(set(keys.values()) == {secret_env}, "switch RADIUS keys match secrets.env RADIUS_SECRET")
        c.check(secret_env != "", "RADIUS_SECRET is not empty")

    client_secrets = re.findall(r"^\s*secret\s*=\s*(\S+)$", clients_conf, re.M)
    c.check(client_secrets and len(set(client_secrets)) == 1, "clients.conf uses one shared secret")
    if client_secrets and secret_env:
        c.check(client_secrets[0] == secret_env, "clients.conf secret matches secrets.env")
        c.check(set(keys.values()) == {client_secrets[0]}, "switch keys match clients.conf")
    for ip in MGMT_IPS.values():
        c.check(f"ipaddr       = {ip}" in clients_conf, f"clients.conf has a client for {ip}")

    for name, (vlan, password) in EXPECTED_USERS.items():
        c.check(name in users, f"users file contains {name}")
        if name not in users:
            continue
        attributes = users[name]
        c.check(
            re.search(r"Tunnel-Type\s*=\s*VLAN", attributes) is not None,
            f"users: {name} has Tunnel-Type VLAN",
        )
        c.check(
            re.search(r"Tunnel-Medium-Type\s*=\s*IEEE-802", attributes) is not None,
            f"users: {name} has Tunnel-Medium-Type IEEE-802",
        )
        match = re.search(r"Tunnel-Private-Group-Id\s*=\s*\"?(\d+)\"?", attributes)
        c.check(match is not None and match.group(1) == vlan,
                f"users: {name} maps to VLAN {vlan}")
        if password:
            match = re.search(r'Cleartext-Password\s*:=\s*"([^"]*)"', attributes)
            c.check(match is not None and match.group(1) == password,

        c.check(mac in users, f"users file contains sensor MAC {mac}")

    # Supplicant profiles
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for name, (vlan, password) in EXPECTED_USERS.items():
        if password is None:
            continue
        path = CLIENTS / f"wpa_supplicant-{name}.conf"
        c.check(path.exists(), f"supplicant config exists for {name}")

        c.check("key_mgmt=IEEE8021X" in text, f"supplicant {name}: IEEE8021X key management")
        c.check("eap=MD5" in text, f"supplicant {name}: EAP-MD5 selected (no certificates needed)")
        c.check("ca_cert" not in text, f"supplicant {name}: no CA certificate required")

    # Docker server segment and sensor
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    c.check("freeradius/freeradius-server" in compose, "compose: FreeRADIUS image")
    c.check("eclipse-mosquitto" in compose, "compose: Mosquitto image")
    c.check("driver: macvlan" in compose, "compose: server segment uses macvlan")
    c.check("192.168.50.10" in compose, "compose: RADIUS container address .10")
    c.check("192.168.50.20" in compose, "compose: MQTT container address .20")
    c.check("gateway: 192.168.50.1" in compose, "compose: gateway is R1 .1")
    c.check("listener 1883 0.0.0.0" in mosquitto, "mosquitto: listener on 1883")
    c.check("allow_anonymous true" in mosquitto, "mosquitto: anonymous access for lab")
    c.check(env.get("RADIUS_IP") == "192.168.50.10", "secrets.env RADIUS_IP matches compose")
    c.check(env.get("MQTT_IP") == "192.168.50.20", "secrets.env MQTT_IP matches compose")

    c.check("5" in str(sensor_py), "sensor: default interval references 5 seconds")

!
! SW3 - Access switch for GUEST (VLAN 30) and IoT (VLAN 40)
! g0/0 trunk to SW1; g0/1 guest 802.1X; g0/2-4 IoT MAB
!
hostname SW3
!
enable secret En4ble-Secret-2026
!
no ip domain lookup
ip domain name campus.local
no ip routing
!
service timestamps debug datetime msec
service timestamps log datetime msec
service password-encryption
!
banner motd #
Campus Network - SW3 Access - Authorized access only
#
!
! ============================================================
! VLAN database
! ============================================================
!
vlan 10
 name STAFF
vlan 20
 name STUDENT
vlan 30
 name GUEST
vlan 40
 name IOT
vlan 99
 name MGMT
!
! ============================================================
! Layer 2 / spanning tree
! ============================================================
!
spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst
!
! ============================================================
! Trunk to SW1
! ============================================================
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 description TRUNK-TO-SW1-G0/2
 switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30,40,99
 switchport nonegotiate
 no shutdown
!
! ============================================================
! GUEST access port - 802.1X, fallback to GUEST VLAN 30
! ============================================================
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 description GUEST-PC1-802.1X
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 30
 switchport nonegotiate
 authentication order dot1x
 authentication port-control auto
 authentication event fail action authorize vlan 30
 authentication event server dead action authorize vlan 30
 authentication event no-response action authorize vlan 30
 dot1x pae authenticator
 spanning-tree portfast
 no shutdown
!
! ============================================================
! IoT access ports.
!
! Design intent is MAB (MAC Authentication Bypass) against RADIUS.
! IOSvL2 accepts the "mab" command but has no working MAB state
! machine: the sensor frames reach the port and the port stays
! unauthorized, no authentication session is ever created. Port
! security with the three known sensor MACs enforces the same rule
! (only these devices may use VLAN 40) on this platform.
!
! On real Catalyst hardware, replace the three
! "switchport port-security*" lines per port with:
!   authentication order mab
!   authentication port-control auto
!   mab
!   dot1x pae authenticator
! The RADIUS side is already prepared: radius/users contains the
! MAB identities 0200.0000.4001 through 0200.0000.4003.
! ============================================================
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/2
 description SENSOR-TEMP
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 40
 switchport nonegotiate
 switchport port-security
 switchport port-security maximum 1
 switchport port-security mac-address 0200.0000.4001
 switchport port-security violation restrict
 spanning-tree portfast
 no shutdown
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/3
 description SENSOR-MOTION
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 40
 switchport nonegotiate
 switchport port-security
 switchport port-security maximum 1
 switchport port-security mac-address 0200.0000.4002
 switchport port-security violation restrict
 spanning-tree portfast
 no shutdown
!
interface GigabitEthernet1/0
 description SENSOR-HUMIDITY
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 40
 switchport nonegotiate
 switchport port-security
 switchport port-security maximum 1
 switchport port-security mac-address 0200.0000.4003
 switchport port-security violation restrict
 spanning-tree portfast
 no shutdown
!
! ============================================================
! Management SVI
! ============================================================
!
interface Vlan99
 description MGMT-SVI
 ip address 192.168.99.13 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
!
ip default-gateway 192.168.99.1
!
! ============================================================
! AAA / RADIUS - SW3 is the 802.1X/MAB authenticator
! ============================================================
!
aaa new-model
aaa authentication login default local
aaa authorization exec default local
!
! T10: after this many failed attempts (time 10s / 2 tries) the server is
! marked dead and 802.1X ports fall back to GUEST VLAN 30 instead of staying
! unauthorized for the whole outage.
radius-server dead-criteria time 10 tries 2
!
radius server RADIUS-1
 address ipv4 192.168.50.10 auth-port 1812 acct-port 1813
 timeout 5
 retransmit 3
 key 0 S3cr3t-Shared-Key-2026
 exit
!
! A named server group is required: a "radius server" definition is not
! automatically a member of the default "radius" group.
aaa group server radius CAMPUS-RADIUS
 server name RADIUS-1
 exit
!
aaa authentication dot1x default group CAMPUS-RADIUS
aaa authorization network default group CAMPUS-RADIUS
aaa accounting dot1x default start-stop group CAMPUS-RADIUS
!
dot1x system-auth-control
ip radius source-interface Vlan99
!
username admin privilege 15 secret En4ble-Secret-2026
!
line con 0
 logging synchronous
line vty 0 4
 logging synchronous
!
end

#      |
#   srv-mac (veth end used as the Docker macvlan parent)
#      |
#   radius .10 / mqtt .20
#
# Why the veth pair? Docker macvlan needs a parent interface, while GNS3's
# Cloud node wants a bridge. Putting a veth pair between them gives each side

display.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Create the Linux-side plumbing for the 192.168.50.0/24 server segment.
#
#   br-srv (Linux bridge)  <-- GNS3 Cloud node -- R1 g0/1
#      |
#   srv-br (veth peer)
#      |
#   srv-mac (veth end used as the Docker macvlan parent)
#      |
#   radius .10 / mqtt .20
#
# Why the veth pair? Docker macvlan needs a parent interface, while GNS3's
# Cloud node wants a bridge. Putting a veth pair between them gives each side
# the interface type it expects.
#
# Run as your normal user; the script uses sudo where required.
set -euo pipefail

BRIDGE="${SERVER_BRIDGE:-br-srv}"
MAC_PARENT="${SERVER_MACVLAN_PARENT:-srv-mac}"
# Keep the documented peer name (srv-br), not "${MAC_PARENT}-br" (srv-mac-br).
# The peer name is independent of the macvlan parent name.
PEER="${SERVER_VETH_PEER:-srv-br}"

if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
    SUDO=""
else
    SUDO="sudo"
fi

if ! command -v ip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: the 'ip' command is required." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if ! ip link show "$BRIDGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Creating bridge $BRIDGE"
    $SUDO ip link add "$BRIDGE" type bridge
else
    echo "Bridge $BRIDGE already exists"
fi
$SUDO ip link set "$BRIDGE" up

if ip link show "$MAC_PARENT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Interface $MAC_PARENT already exists"
    if ! ip link show "$PEER" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "ERROR: $MAC_PARENT exists but its expected peer $PEER does not." >&2
        echo "       Remove $MAC_PARENT or set SERVER_MACVLAN_PARENT to a new name." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
else
    if ip link show "$PEER" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "ERROR: $PEER exists but $MAC_PARENT does not." >&2
        echo "       Remove $PEER or set SERVER_VETH_PEER to a new name." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "Creating veth pair $MAC_PARENT <-> $PEER"
    $SUDO ip link add "$MAC_PARENT" type veth peer name "$PEER"
fi

if ! ip -o link show "$PEER" | grep -q "master $BRIDGE"; then
    $SUDO ip link set "$PEER" master "$BRIDGE"
fi
$SUDO ip link set "$PEER" up
$SUDO ip link set "$MAC_PARENT" up

echo
echo "Server-segment plumbing is ready:"
echo "  bridge      : $BRIDGE   (attach the GNS3 Cloud node here)"
echo "  macvlan base: $MAC_PARENT (used by docker compose)"
echo
echo "Next:"
echo "  cd $(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
echo "  docker compose up -d"
echo
echo "To remove it later:"
echo "  docker compose down"
echo "  sudo ip link del $MAC_PARENT   # also removes $PEER"
echo "  sudo ip link del $BRIDGE"

display.text:
# Server segment for the campus lab.
#
# Networking model:
#   The containers sit on a macvlan network whose parent is srv-mac.
#   srv-mac is one end of a veth pair; the peer (srv-br) is attached to the

name: campus-network

services:

1: # Campus Network - Topology and Addressing
2: 
3: This is the build reference for the GNS3 project. The click-by-click procedure
4: is in [gns3-build-steps.md](gns3-build-steps.md); the firewall/RADIUS policy is
5: implemented in `configs/` and `radius/`.
6: 
7: ## 1. Logical diagram
8: 
9: ```
10:                               8.8.8.8/32 (Loopback0)
11:                                       [R2]
12:                                        | 10.0.0.0/30
13:                                        | R2 .2 / R1 .1
14:                                        |
15:                           [R1  Gateway / Firewall / DHCP / PAT]
16:                          / g0/0 (802.1Q trunk)          g0/1
17:                         /                                \  192.168.50.0/24
18:                   [SW1  Distribution / STP root]          [ SERVER SEGMENT ]
19:                   / g0/1                  \ g0/2            RADIUS 192.168.50.10
20:                  /                          \               MQTT   192.168.50.20
21:             [SW2  Access]                [SW3  Access]      (Docker compose,
22:             /     |      \                |     |    \      reached via GNS3
23:        Gi0/1  Gi0/2  Gi0/3  Gi1/0-2    Gi0/1  Gi0/2-3     Cloud on br-srv)
24:         |      |      |     |             |      |    \
25:    STAFF-PC1 PC2  PC3  STUDENT-PC1..3  GUEST  SENSOR-TEMP
26:                                                   SENSOR-MOTION
27:                                                   SENSOR-HUMIDITY
28: ```
29: 
30: > IOSvL2 exposes eight switch ports as `Gi0/0`-`Gi0/3` plus `Gi1/0`-`Gi1/3`;
31: > there are no `Gi0/4`-`Gi0/6` ports on this image. The fifth to seventh
32: > endpoint links therefore land on the second port group (SW2 students on
33: > `Gi1/0`-`Gi1/2`, SW3 humidity on `Gi1/0`). GNS3 adapter 0-3 maps to
34: > `Gi0/0`-`Gi0/3` and adapter 4-7 maps to `Gi1/0`-`Gi1/3`.
35: 
36: VLANs are carried as 802.1Q tags on all inter-switch and R1-SW1 links:
37: `10,20,30,40,99`. The server segment is a separate routed subnet; it is not a
38: VLAN on the switch trunk.
39: 
40: ## 2. Node inventory
41: 
42: | Node | GNS3 type | Role | Notes |
43: |---|---|---|---|
44: | R1 | Cisco IOSv | Campus gateway, DHCP, NAT/PAT, ACL firewall | 3 interfaces used: g0/0, g0/1, g0/2 |
45: | R2 | Cisco IOSv | Simulated ISP / Internet | Loopback0 = 8.8.8.8/32 |
46: | SW1 | Cisco IOSvL2 | Distribution, rapid-PVST root | 3 trunk ports, no access ports |
47: | SW2 | Cisco IOSvL2 | STAFF + STUDENT access | 802.1X authenticator |
48: | SW3 | Cisco IOSvL2 | GUEST + IoT access | 802.1X authenticator; IoT ports use port security (see note below) |
49: | STAFF-PC1..3 | Docker `campus-client:1.0` | Staff endpoints | wpa_supplicant, EAP-MD5 |
50: | STUDENT-PC1..3 | Docker `campus-client:1.0` | Student endpoints | wpa_supplicant, EAP-MD5 |
51: | GUEST-PC1 | Docker `campus-client:1.0` | Guest endpoint | wpa_supplicant, EAP-MD5 |
52: | SENSOR-TEMP | Docker `campus-sensor:1.0` | Temperature sensor | VLAN 40, MAC 0200.0000.4001 |
53: | SENSOR-MOTION | Docker `campus-sensor:1.0` | Motion sensor | VLAN 40, MAC 0200.0000.4002 |
54: | SENSOR-HUMIDITY | Docker `campus-sensor:1.0` | Humidity sensor | VLAN 40, MAC 0200.0000.4003 |
55: | SERVER-CLOUD | GNS3 Cloud | Link to `br-srv` | R1 g0/1 attaches here |
56: | RADIUS | Docker compose | FreeRADIUS 3.2.3 | 192.168.50.10 |
57: | MQTT | Docker compose | Eclipse Mosquitto 2.x | 192.168.50.20 |
58: 
59: The RADIUS and MQTT containers are not GNS3 nodes. They run on the Docker host
60: and are reached through the SERVER-CLOUD link. See `radius/docker-compose.yml`
61: and `radius/setup-server-bridge.sh`.
62: 
63: ## 3. Port map
64: 
65: | Link | Ports | Mode / VLAN | Endpoint |
66: |---|---|---|---|
67: | R1 <-> SW1 | R1 g0/0 <-> SW1 g0/0 | 802.1Q trunk, VLANs 10,20,30,40,99 | Router-on-a-stick |
68: | SW1 <-> SW2 | SW1 g0/1 <-> SW2 g0/0 | 802.1Q trunk | Distribution to access |
69: | SW1 <-> SW3 | SW1 g0/2 <-> SW3 g0/0 | 802.1Q trunk | Distribution to access |
70: | SW2 staff 1 | SW2 g0/1 | Access VLAN 10, 802.1X | STAFF-PC1 |
71: | SW2 staff 2 | SW2 g0/2 | Access VLAN 10, 802.1X | STAFF-PC2 |
72: | SW2 staff 3 | SW2 g0/3 | Access VLAN 10, 802.1X | STAFF-PC3 |
73: | SW2 student 1 | SW2 Gi1/0 | Access VLAN 20, 802.1X | STUDENT-PC1 |
74: | SW2 student 2 | SW2 Gi1/1 | Access VLAN 20, 802.1X | STUDENT-PC2 |
75: | SW2 student 3 | SW2 Gi1/2 | Access VLAN 20, 802.1X | STUDENT-PC3 |
76: | SW3 guest | SW3 Gi0/1 | Access VLAN 30, 802.1X | GUEST-PC1 |
77: | SW3 IoT temp | SW3 Gi0/2 | Access VLAN 40, port security | SENSOR-TEMP |
78: | SW3 IoT motion | SW3 Gi0/3 | Access VLAN 40, port security | SENSOR-MOTION |
79: | SW3 IoT humidity | SW3 Gi1/0 | Access VLAN 40, port security | SENSOR-HUMIDITY |
80: | R1 <-> server | R1 g0/1 <-> SERVER-CLOUD (`br-srv`) | Routed 192.168.50.0/24 | RADIUS + MQTT |
81: | R1 <-> R2 | R1 g0/2 <-> R2 g0/0 | Routed 10.0.0.0/30 | Simulated ISP |
82: 
83: On SW2 and SW3 the initial `switchport access vlan` is the "pre-auth" VLAN:
84: 10 for staff ports, 20 for student ports, 30 for guest, 40 for IoT. After a
85: successful RADIUS exchange the switch moves the port to the VLAN returned in
86: `Tunnel-Private-Group-Id` (normally the same VLAN, which makes the assignment
87: visible in `show authentication sessions`). A failed/no-response 802.1X user
88: port is authorized into VLAN 30 (guest fallback).
89: 
90: IoT ports are configured with port security instead of MAB: IOSvL2 accepts the
91: `mab` command but never creates an authentication session, so a MAB port stays
92: permanently unauthorized. Each sensor port pins the sensor MAC
93: (`switchport port-security mac-address 0200.0000.40xx`) with a maximum of one
94: address and `violation restrict`, which keeps unknown devices off VLAN 40. The
95: RADIUS server is still configured for MAB identities, so the same `users` file
96: works when the configs are pasted onto Catalyst hardware; see the note in
97: `configs/SW3.cfg` for the four lines to swap back.
98: 
99: ## 4. Addressing
100: 
101: | VLAN | Name | Subnet | Gateway | DHCP pool | Notes |
102: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
103: | 10 | STAFF | 192.168.10.0/24 | 192.168.10.1 | .21-.254 | 3 Docker clients, full access |
104: | 20 | STUDENT | 192.168.20.0/24 | 192.168.20.1 | .21-.254 | 3 Docker clients, Internet only |
105: | 30 | GUEST | 192.168.30.0/24 | 192.168.30.1 | .21-.254 | 1 Docker client + fallback |
106: | 40 | IOT | 192.168.40.0/24 | 192.168.40.1 | .21-.254 | 3 Docker sensors, MQTT only |
107: | 99 | MGMT | 192.168.99.0/24 | 192.168.99.1 | static | SW1 .11, SW2 .12, SW3 .13 |
108: | - | SERVER | 192.168.50.0/24 | 192.168.50.1 | static | RADIUS .10, MQTT .20 |
109: | - | R1-R2 | 10.0.0.0/30 | - | - | R1 .1, R2 .2 |
110: | - | Internet sim | 8.8.8.8/32 | - | - | R2 Loopback0 |
111: 
112: DHCP is served by R1 on the VLAN 10/20/30/40 subinterfaces. Each pool excludes
113: `.1` through `.20`; clients receive `.21` and above. DNS option is `8.8.8.8`
114: (the simulated Internet host); see the test plan for the DNS caveat.
115: 
116: ### Management addresses
117: 
118: | Device | Interface | Address | Default gateway |
119: |---|---|---|---|
120: | R1 | g0/0.99 | 192.168.99.1/24 | - |
121: | SW1 | Vlan99 | 192.168.99.11/24 | 192.168.99.1 |
122: | SW2 | Vlan99 | 192.168.99.12/24 | 192.168.99.1 |
123: | SW3 | Vlan99 | 192.168.99.13/24 | 192.168.99.1 |
124: 
125: ### Fixed sensor MACs
126: 
127: | Sensor | MAC | RADIUS user | VLAN |
128: |---|---|---|---|
