# Campus Network - Topology and Addressing

This is the build reference for the GNS3 project. The click-by-click procedure
is in [gns3-build-steps.md](gns3-build-steps.md); the firewall/RADIUS policy is
implemented in `configs/` and `radius/`.

## 1. Logical diagram

```
                              8.8.8.8/32 (Loopback0)
                                      [R2]
                                       | 10.0.0.0/30
                                       | R2 .2 / R1 .1
                                       |
                          [R1  Gateway / Firewall / DHCP / PAT]
                         / g0/0 (802.1Q trunk)          g0/1
                        /                                \  192.168.50.0/24
                  [SW1  Distribution / STP root]          [ SERVER SEGMENT ]
                  / g0/1                  \ g0/2            RADIUS 192.168.50.10
                 /                          \               MQTT   192.168.50.20
            [SW2  Access]                [SW3  Access]      (Docker compose,
            /     |      \                |     |    \      reached via GNS3
       Gi0/1  Gi0/2  Gi0/3  Gi1/0-2    Gi0/1  Gi0/2-3     Cloud on br-srv)
        |      |      |     |             |      |    \
   STAFF-PC1 PC2  PC3  STUDENT-PC1..3  GUEST  SENSOR-TEMP
                                                  SENSOR-MOTION
                                                  SENSOR-HUMIDITY
```

> IOSvL2 exposes eight switch ports as `Gi0/0`-`Gi0/3` plus `Gi1/0`-`Gi1/3`;
> there are no `Gi0/4`-`Gi0/6` ports on this image. The fifth to seventh
> endpoint links therefore land on the second port group (SW2 students on
> `Gi1/0`-`Gi1/2`, SW3 humidity on `Gi1/0`). GNS3 adapter 0-3 maps to
> `Gi0/0`-`Gi0/3` and adapter 4-7 maps to `Gi1/0`-`Gi1/3`.

VLANs are carried as 802.1Q tags on all inter-switch and R1-SW1 links:
`10,20,30,40,99`. The server segment is a separate routed subnet; it is not a
VLAN on the switch trunk.

## 2. Node inventory

| Node | GNS3 type | Role | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Cisco IOSv | Campus gateway, DHCP, NAT/PAT, ACL firewall | 3 interfaces used: g0/0, g0/1, g0/2 |
| R2 | Cisco IOSv | Simulated ISP / Internet | Loopback0 = 8.8.8.8/32 |
| SW1 | Cisco IOSvL2 | Distribution, rapid-PVST root | 3 trunk ports, no access ports |
| SW2 | Cisco IOSvL2 | STAFF + STUDENT access | 802.1X authenticator |
| SW3 | Cisco IOSvL2 | GUEST + IoT access | 802.1X authenticator; IoT ports use port security (see note below) |
| STAFF-PC1..3 | Docker `campus-client:1.0` | Staff endpoints | wpa_supplicant, EAP-MD5 |
| STUDENT-PC1..3 | Docker `campus-client:1.0` | Student endpoints | wpa_supplicant, EAP-MD5 |
| GUEST-PC1 | Docker `campus-client:1.0` | Guest endpoint | wpa_supplicant, EAP-MD5 |
| SENSOR-TEMP | Docker `campus-sensor:1.0` | Temperature sensor | VLAN 40, MAC 0200.0000.4001 |
| SENSOR-MOTION | Docker `campus-sensor:1.0` | Motion sensor | VLAN 40, MAC 0200.0000.4002 |
| SENSOR-HUMIDITY | Docker `campus-sensor:1.0` | Humidity sensor | VLAN 40, MAC 0200.0000.4003 |
| SERVER-CLOUD | GNS3 Cloud | Link to `br-srv` | R1 g0/1 attaches here |
| RADIUS | Docker compose | FreeRADIUS 3.2.3 | 192.168.50.10 |
| MQTT | Docker compose | Eclipse Mosquitto 2.x | 192.168.50.20 |

The RADIUS and MQTT containers are not GNS3 nodes. They run on the Docker host
and are reached through the SERVER-CLOUD link. See `radius/docker-compose.yml`
and `radius/setup-server-bridge.sh`.

## 3. Port map

| Link | Ports | Mode / VLAN | Endpoint |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 <-> SW1 | R1 g0/0 <-> SW1 g0/0 | 802.1Q trunk, VLANs 10,20,30,40,99 | Router-on-a-stick |
| SW1 <-> SW2 | SW1 g0/1 <-> SW2 g0/0 | 802.1Q trunk | Distribution to access |
| SW1 <-> SW3 | SW1 g0/2 <-> SW3 g0/0 | 802.1Q trunk | Distribution to access |
| SW2 staff 1 | SW2 g0/1 | Access VLAN 10, 802.1X | STAFF-PC1 |
| SW2 staff 2 | SW2 g0/2 | Access VLAN 10, 802.1X | STAFF-PC2 |
| SW2 staff 3 | SW2 g0/3 | Access VLAN 10, 802.1X | STAFF-PC3 |
| SW2 student 1 | SW2 Gi1/0 | Access VLAN 20, 802.1X | STUDENT-PC1 |
| SW2 student 2 | SW2 Gi1/1 | Access VLAN 20, 802.1X | STUDENT-PC2 |
| SW2 student 3 | SW2 Gi1/2 | Access VLAN 20, 802.1X | STUDENT-PC3 |
| SW3 guest | SW3 Gi0/1 | Access VLAN 30, 802.1X | GUEST-PC1 |
| SW3 IoT temp | SW3 Gi0/2 | Access VLAN 40, port security | SENSOR-TEMP |
| SW3 IoT motion | SW3 Gi0/3 | Access VLAN 40, port security | SENSOR-MOTION |
| SW3 IoT humidity | SW3 Gi1/0 | Access VLAN 40, port security | SENSOR-HUMIDITY |
| R1 <-> server | R1 g0/1 <-> SERVER-CLOUD (`br-srv`) | Routed 192.168.50.0/24 | RADIUS + MQTT |
| R1 <-> R2 | R1 g0/2 <-> R2 g0/0 | Routed 10.0.0.0/30 | Simulated ISP |

On SW2 and SW3 the initial `switchport access vlan` is the "pre-auth" VLAN:
10 for staff ports, 20 for student ports, 30 for guest, 40 for IoT. After a
successful RADIUS exchange the switch moves the port to the VLAN returned in
`Tunnel-Private-Group-Id` (normally the same VLAN, which makes the assignment
visible in `show authentication sessions`). A failed/no-response 802.1X user
port is authorized into VLAN 30 (guest fallback).

IoT ports are configured with port security instead of MAB: IOSvL2 accepts the
`mab` command but never creates an authentication session, so a MAB port stays
permanently unauthorized. Each sensor port pins the sensor MAC
(`switchport port-security mac-address 0200.0000.40xx`) with a maximum of one
address and `violation restrict`, which keeps unknown devices off VLAN 40. The
RADIUS server is still configured for MAB identities, so the same `users` file
works when the configs are pasted onto Catalyst hardware; see the note in
`configs/SW3.cfg` for the four lines to swap back.

## 4. Addressing

| VLAN | Name | Subnet | Gateway | DHCP pool | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | STAFF | 192.168.10.0/24 | 192.168.10.1 | .21-.254 | 3 Docker clients, full access |
| 20 | STUDENT | 192.168.20.0/24 | 192.168.20.1 | .21-.254 | 3 Docker clients, Internet only |
| 30 | GUEST | 192.168.30.0/24 | 192.168.30.1 | .21-.254 | 1 Docker client + fallback |
| 40 | IOT | 192.168.40.0/24 | 192.168.40.1 | .21-.254 | 3 Docker sensors, MQTT only |
| 99 | MGMT | 192.168.99.0/24 | 192.168.99.1 | static | SW1 .11, SW2 .12, SW3 .13 |
| - | SERVER | 192.168.50.0/24 | 192.168.50.1 | static | RADIUS .10, MQTT .20 |
| - | R1-R2 | 10.0.0.0/30 | - | - | R1 .1, R2 .2 |
| - | Internet sim | 8.8.8.8/32 | - | - | R2 Loopback0 |

DHCP is served by R1 on the VLAN 10/20/30/40 subinterfaces. Each pool excludes
`.1` through `.20`; clients receive `.21` and above. DNS option is `8.8.8.8`
(the simulated Internet host); see the test plan for the DNS caveat.

### Management addresses

| Device | Interface | Address | Default gateway |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | g0/0.99 | 192.168.99.1/24 | - |
| SW1 | Vlan99 | 192.168.99.11/24 | 192.168.99.1 |
| SW2 | Vlan99 | 192.168.99.12/24 | 192.168.99.1 |
| SW3 | Vlan99 | 192.168.99.13/24 | 192.168.99.1 |

### Fixed sensor MACs

| Sensor | MAC | RADIUS user | VLAN |
|---|---|---|---|
| Temperature | 0200.0000.4001 | 0200.0000.4001 | 40 |
| Motion | 0200.0000.4002 | 0200.0000.4002 | 40 |
| Humidity | 0200.0000.4003 | 0200.0000.4003 | 40 |

These MACs must be set on the GNS3 Docker nodes (or via `SENSOR_MAC`) so the
switch port-security entry and the RADIUS MAB identity both match. `radius/users` includes dotted, plain, hyphen and colon
aliases; if the switch sends a format not listed there, add one alias as
described in the README.

## 5. VLAN/STP design

- `spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst` on all switches.
- SW1 is `root primary` for VLANs 10,20,30,40,99.
- SW2/SW3 are access switches; all their uplinks are trunks.
- Access ports use `spanning-tree portfast`.
- Native VLAN is left at VLAN 1 on the trunks; only tagged VLANs 10,20,30,40,99
  are allowed. No user traffic is placed in VLAN 1.

## 6. Server segment wiring

The Docker segment is deliberately separated from the switch fabric:

```
R1 g0/1 --- GNS3 Cloud (br-srv)
                        |
                  srv-br (veth peer)
                        |
                  srv-mac (macvlan parent)
                   /          \
             radius .10     mqtt .20
```

`radius/setup-server-bridge.sh` creates the bridge and veth pair. The compose
network uses `srv-mac` as its macvlan parent and `192.168.50.1` as the
containers' gateway, which is R1. This keeps R1 as the only router/firewall for
the server segment and avoids putting a Docker bridge IP on 192.168.50.1.

## 7. Traffic policy summary

| Source VLAN | Allowed | Denied |
|---|---|---|
| STAFF (10) | Everything: Internet, SERVER, STUDENT, IOT, MGMT | none |
| STUDENT (20) | DHCP, gateway echo, Internet DNS/HTTP/HTTPS | all RFC1918 reached through R1 (STAFF, IOT, MGMT, SERVER) |
| GUEST (30) | DHCP, gateway echo, Internet DNS/HTTP/HTTPS | all RFC1918 |
| IOT (40) | DHCP, DNS to 8.8.8.8, MQTT tcp/1883 to 192.168.50.20 | Internet, all other internal ranges |
| MGMT (99) | RADIUS udp/1812,1813 to 192.168.50.10; echo replies and established TCP for sessions opened by STAFF | everything else (switches cannot initiate outbound traffic) |

The ACLs are named extended ACLs on R1: `STAFF_IN`, `STUDENT_IN`, `GUEST_IN`,
`IOT_IN`, `MGMT_IN`, each applied inbound on its VLAN subinterface and ending
with `deny ip any any log`. They filter only traffic that is routed through
R1; two hosts in the same VLAN exchange frames through the access switch and
do not hit these ACLs. Add private VLANs or `switchport protected` if
same-VLAN peer isolation is required.

220:    ```
221: 
222: 2. On SW3:
223: 
224:    ```text
225:    show port-security
226:    show port-security interface GigabitEthernet0/2
227:    show mac address-table | include 0200.0000.40
228:    ```
229: 
230: 3. Confirm the sensors have 192.168.40.x leases (`ip addr show eth0` in each
231:    container) and publish to the broker (T16).
232: 
233: **Expected:** Each IoT port is `Secure-up`, maximum 1 address, `Restrict`,
234: with `Last Source Address:Vlan` equal to the sensor MAC in VLAN 40. The MAC
235: table shows the three addresses as `STATIC` in VLAN 40. Each sensor has a
236: 192.168.40.x lease.
237: 
238: **Steps (hardware MAB variant):**
239: 
240: 1. Replace the port-security lines on each IoT port with
241:    `authentication order mab`, `authentication port-control auto`, `mab` and
242:    `dot1x pae authenticator`.
243: 2. `show authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet0/2 details` shows
244:    method `mab`, status `Auth`, VLAN 40.
245: 3. In RADIUS debug, the Access-Request User-Name is `0200.0000.4001`
246:    (or one of the aliases in `radius/users`), and the Access-Accept contains
247:    `Tunnel-Private-Group-Id = "40"`.
248: 
249: **Evidence:** `report/evidence/T06-T07-sw3-sessions.txt` (port security,
250: sessions, MAC table), sensor leases, and `T16-mqtt-subscribe.txt`.
251: 
252: ### T08 - Moving staff1 to another port keeps VLAN 10
253: 
254: **Where:** SW2 g0/1 and g0/3.
255: 
256: **Steps:**
257: 
258: 1. With STAFF-PC1 authenticated on g0/1, delete the GNS3 link from SW2 g0/1.
259: 2. Connect STAFF-PC1 itself to SW2 g0/3 (move its link), or use a spare client
260:    configured with the staff1 profile. Do not use STAFF-PC3's staff3 profile
261:    for this test.
262: 3. If the port does not restart authentication, on SW2:
263: 
264:    ```text
265:    interface GigabitEthernet0/3
266:     shutdown
267:     no shutdown
268:    ```
269: 
270: 4. Run `show authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet0/3 details`.
271: 
272: **Expected:** The new port authenticates the same staff1 identity and is
273: authorized in VLAN 10 with a 192.168.10.x address. The old port has no active
274: session. This proves the VLAN comes from RADIUS, not from the port's static
275: access VLAN (both staff ports start in VLAN 10, so also show the RADIUS
276: Access-Accept for the new session).
277: 
278: **Evidence:** Session output on g0/3, DHCP address, RADIUS debug for the new
279: NAS port.
280: 
281: ### T09 - Wrong password -> guest fallback VLAN 30
282: 
283: **Where:** a spare client using `wpa_supplicant-wrongpass.conf`, SW2, RADIUS.
284: 
285: **Steps:**
286: 
287: 1. Connect the spare client to a staff port (for example g0/2) with the
288:    wrong-password profile. Build/use a client image whose `WPA_CONF` points at
289:    `/etc/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant-wrongpass.conf`.
290: 2. Watch `show authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet0/2 details`
291:    and the RADIUS debug.
292: 3. Check the client's DHCP address: `ip addr show eth0`.
293: 
294: **Expected:** RADIUS returns `Access-Reject` for staff1. SW2 applies
295: `authentication event fail action authorize vlan 30`; the port is authorized
296: in **VLAN 30**, and the client gets a 192.168.30.x address. It can reach the
297: Internet but cannot ping 192.168.10.x, 192.168.40.x, 192.168.50.x or
298: 192.168.99.x (guest ACL).
299: 
300: **Evidence:** Access-Reject, session output showing VLAN 30, guest DHCP lease,
301: failed internal pings.
302: 
303: ### T10 - RADIUS server dead -> guest fallback VLAN 30
304: 
305: **Where:** STAFF-PC3 on SW2 `Gi0/3`, Docker host.
306: 
307: **Steps:**
308: 
309: 1. Stop RADIUS: `docker stop radius` (or `docker compose stop radius`).
310: 2. Force a fresh authentication attempt. Re-authentication on an already
311:    authorized port does not test this path, because IOS keeps the last known
312:    good session when a *re-auth* times out. Clear the session and restart
313:    EAPOL instead:
314:    - SW2: `clear authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet0/3`
315:    - client: `wpa_cli -i eth0 reassociate`
316:      (or stop/start the endpoint in GNS3)
317: 3. Wait for the dead criteria: `radius-server dead-criteria time 10 tries 2`
318:    with `timeout 5` / `retransmit 3` marks the server dead in roughly 30-60s.
319: 4. Check `show aaa servers` (`Dead: ... count`), `show logging` for
320:    `%RADIUS-4-RADIUS_DEAD`, and
321:    `show interface GigabitEthernet0/3 switchport` (`Access Mode VLAN: 30`).
322: 5. Renew DHCP on the client and test the guest ACL.
323: 6. Restart RADIUS (`docker start radius`), clear the session and reassociate;
324:    confirm the port returns to VLAN 10.
325: 
326: **Expected:** While RADIUS is unreachable, the port is authorized in **VLAN 30**
327: by `authentication event server dead action authorize vlan 30`, and the client
328: gets a 192.168.30.x lease. As in T09, HTTP to 8.8.8.8 succeeds while staff,
329: RADIUS, MQTT and MGMT destinations are blocked by `GUEST_IN`.
330: 
331: **Note:** `authentication event no-response` is about a silent *supplicant*,
332: not a silent RADIUS server; it is not the right event for a RADIUS outage.
333: `authentication event server dead` is the working fallback on this image.
334: 
335: **Evidence:** `T10-server-dead.txt` - dead counter, `RADIUS_DEAD` syslog,
336: session in VLAN 30, 192.168.30.22 lease, HTTP 401, blocked internal probes.
337: 
338: ## 4. Firewall policy tests
339: 
340: Run each row from the named endpoint. Use `ping` for ICMP rows and `curl` for
341: HTTP rows. A "pass" means the expected protocol succeeds; "fail" means it is
342: blocked by R1, not merely that an application is absent. For DNS and HTTPS,
343: there is no service on the simulated Internet, so the pass criterion is the
344: ACL permit counter incrementing (T17) rather than an application response.
345: 
346: ### T11 - STAFF ACL matrix
347: 
348: **Where:** STAFF-PC1.
349: 
350: | # | Destination | Command | Expected |
351: |---|---|---|---|
352: | 1 | 8.8.8.8 | `ping -c 3 8.8.8.8` | Pass (NAT to Internet) |
353: | 2 | 8.8.8.8:80 | `curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://8.8.8.8/` | Pass (HTTP code, 401 is acceptable) |
354: | 3 | 192.168.50.10 | `ping -c 3 192.168.50.10` | Pass |
355: | 4 | 192.168.50.20 | `ping -c 3 192.168.50.20` | Pass |
356: | 5 | 192.168.20.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.20.21` | Pass |
357: | 6 | 192.168.40.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.40.21` | Pass |
358: | 7 | 192.168.99.11 | `ping -c 3 192.168.99.11` | Pass |
359: | 8 | 192.168.30.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.30.21` | Pass |
360: 
361: If a student/IoT/guest endpoint is not at `.21`, use its actual DHCP address
362: from T04. Staff has no deny rules, so all rows should succeed.
363: 
364: **Evidence:** Command output for all rows, `show access-lists` on R1 showing
365: STAFF_IN permit counters.
366: 
367: ### T12 - STUDENT ACL matrix
368: 
369: **Where:** STUDENT-PC1.
370: 
371: | # | Destination | Command | Expected |
372: |---|---|---|---|
373: | 1 | 8.8.8.8 | `ping -c 3 8.8.8.8` | Fail (ICMP is not in the student allow-list; use HTTP row 2) |
374: | 2 | 8.8.8.8:80 | `curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://8.8.8.8/` | Pass (HTTP code) |
375: | 3 | 8.8.8.8:443 | `curl -k -sS -m 5 https://8.8.8.8/` | ACL permits; no HTTPS listener, so connection fails. Confirm STUDENT_IN permit counter increments. |
376: | 4 | 8.8.8.8:53 | `nslookup example.com 8.8.8.8` | ACL permits; no DNS listener, so timeout. Confirm permit counter increments. |
377: | 5 | 192.168.10.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.10.21` | Fail (STAFF denied) |
378: | 6 | 192.168.40.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.40.21` | Fail (IOT denied) |
379: | 7 | 192.168.99.11 | `ping -c 3 192.168.99.11` | Fail (MGMT denied) |
380: | 8 | 192.168.50.10 | `ping -c 3 192.168.50.10` | Fail (SERVER denied) |
381: | 9 | 192.168.50.20 | `ping -c 3 192.168.50.20` | Fail (SERVER/MQTT denied) |
382: 
383: > A ping between two hosts in VLAN 20 (for example student1 to student2) is
384: > **not** in this matrix. That traffic is switched by SW2 and never reaches
385: > R1's `STUDENT_IN` ACL, so it succeeds. The ACLs enforce inter-VLAN policy;
386: > same-VLAN peer isolation would require private VLANs or `switchport
387: > protected` on the access ports, which is outside this brief.
388: 
389: **Evidence:** Output for all rows; R1 `show access-lists` STUDENT_IN deny
390: counters for rows 5-9.
391: 
392: ### T13 - GUEST ACL matrix
393: 
394: **Where:** GUEST-PC1.
395: 
396: | # | Destination | Command | Expected |
397: |---|---|---|---|
398: | 1 | 8.8.8.8 | `ping -c 3 8.8.8.8` | Fail (ICMP is not in the guest allow-list) |
399: | 2 | 8.8.8.8:80 | `curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://8.8.8.8/` | Pass (HTTP code) |
400: | 3 | 192.168.10.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.10.21` | Fail |
401: | 4 | 192.168.20.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.20.21` | Fail |
402: | 5 | 192.168.40.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.40.21` | Fail |
403: | 6 | 192.168.50.10 | `ping -c 3 192.168.50.10` | Fail |
404: | 7 | 192.168.99.11 | `ping -c 3 192.168.99.11` | Fail |
405: 
406: **Evidence:** Output for all rows; GUEST_IN deny counters.
407: 
408: ### T14 - IOT ACL matrix
409: 
410: **Where:** each sensor container (SENSOR-TEMP/MOTION/HUMIDITY), SW3.
411: 
412: | # | Destination | Command | Expected |
413: |---|---|---|---|
414: | 1 | 192.168.50.20:1883 | MQTT publish is automatic; verify with T16 | Pass |
415: | 2 | 8.8.8.8 | `ping -c 3 8.8.8.8` | Fail (Internet denied) |
416: | 3 | 8.8.8.8:80 | `wget -T 5 -O /dev/null http://8.8.8.8/` | Fail (Internet denied) |
417: | 4 | 8.8.8.8:53 | `nslookup example.com 8.8.8.8` | ACL permits DNS; no DNS listener, so timeout. Confirm IOT_IN permit counter. |
418: | 5 | 192.168.50.10 | `ping -c 3 192.168.50.10` | Fail (RADIUS not an IoT destination) |
419: | 6 | 192.168.50.10:1812 | `nc -z -w 3 192.168.50.10 1812` (if nc exists) or rely on ACL counter | Fail |
420: | 7 | 192.168.10.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.10.21` | Fail |
421: | 8 | 192.168.20.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.20.21` | Fail |
422: | 9 | 192.168.40.1 | `ping -c 3 192.168.40.1` | Fail (internal/gateway; IOT_IN denies) |
423: 
424: **Evidence:** `ping`/`wget` output from each sensor, `show access-lists`
425: IOT_IN counters showing 1883 permits and deny counters.
426: 
427: ### T15 - MGMT ACL and RADIUS-only access
428: 
429: **Where:** SW2 (MGMT VLAN 99), R1.
430: 
431: **Steps:**
432: 
433: 1. On SW2, test RADIUS reachability:
434: 
435:    ```text
436:    test aaa group CAMPUS-RADIUS staff1 Staff1Pass! legacy
437:    show radius statistics
438:    ```
439: 
440: 2. Try to reach the Internet and MQTT from the switch's management SVI:
441: 
442:    ```text
443:    ping 8.8.8.8
444:    ping 192.168.50.20
445:    ```
446: 
447: 3. Try to ping a staff endpoint from SW2:
448: 
449:    ```text
450:    ping 192.168.10.21
451:    ```
452: 
453: **Expected:** `test aaa` reports successful authentication (or at least a
454: RADIUS Access-Accept and non-zero auth counters); `show radius statistics`
455: shows requests/responses. Pings to 8.8.8.8, 192.168.50.20 and 192.168.10.21
456: fail (packets from VLAN 99 are denied by `MGMT_IN`). RADIUS still works because
457: UDP 1812/1813 to 192.168.50.10 is explicitly permitted.
458: 
459: > `MGMT_IN` also permits ICMP echo replies and established TCP so that staff
460: > (which `STAFF_IN` allows to reach MGMT) can ping or SSH to the switch SVIs.
461: > Switch-originated echo requests and TCP SYNs do not match those entries and
462: > are still denied, which is what this test checks.
463: >
464: > If `test aaa` is unsupported on your IOSvL2 image, the live 802.1X tests
465: > (T05-T09) already prove MGMT-to-RADIUS reachability; capture
466: > `show radius statistics` instead.
467: 
468: **Evidence:** `test aaa` output, `show radius statistics`, failed ping output,
469: MGMT_IN counters.
470: 
471: ## 5. MQTT and sensor tests
472: 
473: ### T16 - All three sensors publish to the broker
474: 
475: **Where:** Docker host, MQTT container.
476: 
477: **Steps:**
478: 
479: 1. Confirm all three sensor containers are running and have 192.168.40.x
480:    addresses.
481: 2. Subscribe for at least 9 messages (3 sensors x 3 samples at 5-second
482:    intervals):
483: 
484:    ```sh
485:    docker exec -it mqtt mosquitto_sub \
486:      -h 127.0.0.1 -t 'campus/iot/#' -v -C 9
487:    ```
488: 
489: 3. Save the output. Each line should be `campus/iot/<id> {"id":...}`.
490: 
491: **Expected:** Messages from `temp-01`, `motion-01` and `humidity-01` arrive
492: within 30 seconds. Payloads are JSON with `id`, `type`, `value`, `timestamp`;
493: types are `temperature`, `motion`, `humidity`; values are plausible (18-26,
494: 0/1, 35-65). No sensor can ping 8.8.8.8 (T14 row 2), proving the IoT ACL does
495: not accidentally permit general Internet access.
496: 
497: **Evidence:** `mosquitto_sub` output with at least 9 lines, sensor logs,
498: sensor `ip addr`, failed Internet ping from one sensor.
499: 
500: ### T17 - ACL hit counters
501: 
502: **Where:** R1.
503: 
504: **Steps:**
505: 
506: 1. Before tests: `clear ip access-list counters` (or note the current counts).
507: 2. Run the T11-T15 matrix.
508: 3. `show access-lists`.
509: 4. `show logging | include ACL|denied` (the ACL entries use `log`).
510: 
511: **Expected:** `STAFF_IN` has high permit counts and no denies; `STUDENT_IN`,
512: `GUEST_IN`, `IOT_IN` and `MGMT_IN` each show both permits for allowed traffic
513: and nonzero denies for the blocked rows. The final `deny ip any any log` entry
514: has a nonzero count when a test hit an unlisted destination. Log entries show
515: the source/destination and the ACL name.
516: 
517: **Evidence:** `show access-lists` before/after, `show logging` excerpt.
518: 
519: ### T18 - NAT/PAT
520: 
521: **Where:** R1, STAFF-PC1/STUDENT-PC1/GUEST-PC1.
522: 
523: **Steps:**
524: 
525: 1. From STAFF-PC1, `ping -c 3 8.8.8.8`.
526: 2. From STUDENT-PC1 and GUEST-PC1, use
527:    `curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://8.8.8.8/`
528:    (their ACLs do not permit ICMP).
529: 3. On R1: `show ip nat translations`, `show ip nat statistics`.
530: 4. From an IoT sensor, attempt `ping 8.8.8.8`, then check NAT again.
531: 
532: **Expected:** Staff, student and guest flows appear as translations from
533: 10.0.0.1 to 8.8.8.8; IoT produces no translation because its ACL drops the
534: packet before NAT. Server/MGMT traffic is not translated.
535: 
536: **Evidence:** NAT translation table, NAT statistics, IoT failed ping.
537: 
538: ## 6. Supporting tests
539: 
540: ### T19 - Spanning tree
541: 
542: **Where:** SW1, SW2, SW3.
543: 
544: **Steps:**
545: 
546: ```text
547: show spanning-tree vlan 10
548: show spanning-tree vlan 20
549: show spanning-tree vlan 30
550: show spanning-tree vlan 40
551: show spanning-tree vlan 99
552: show spanning-tree summary
553: ```
554: 
555: **Expected:** SW1 is root for all five VLANs; SW2/SW3 reach SW1 through a root
556: port on g0/0; no access port is blocking; rapid-pvst is active.
557: 
558: **Evidence:** `show spanning-tree` output from each switch.
559: 
560: ### T20 - Configuration persistence
561: 
562: **Where:** all five Cisco devices.
563: 
564: **Steps:**
565: 
566: 1. `write memory` on each device.
567: 2. `show startup-config | include hostname|radius|access-list|vlan`.
568: 3. Optional: `reload` one switch, wait for boot, and confirm
569:    `show authentication sessions` and `show vlan brief` after reconnecting a
570:    client.
571: 
572: **Expected:** Startup config matches the running config; VLANs, ACLs, RADIUS
573: key and 802.1X settings survive a reload.
574: 
575: **Evidence:** `show startup-config` excerpts, post-reload session output.
576: 
577: ## 7. Pass/fail summary sheet
578: 
579: Copy this into the report and fill it in:
580: 
581: | Test | Result (Pass/Fail) | Evidence file |

display.text:
# Test Plan and Evidence Capture

Every test below maps to a requirement in the assignment brief. The expected
results assume the configs in `configs/` and `radius/` are loaded unchanged.

## 0. Conventions

- Run commands on the device named in **Where**.
- Save evidence as `report/evidence/Txx-short-name.png` (screenshot) or
  `report/evidence/Txx-short-name.txt` (copied console output).
- Endpoint containers are GNS3 Docker nodes. Find their Docker names with:

  ```sh
  docker ps --format 'table {{.Names}}\t{{.Image}}\t{{.Status}}'
  ```

  Then enter one with `docker exec -it <name> sh`. GNS3 may name containers
  differently from the node labels; match on the image name.
- `ping -c 3 -W 2 <ip>` works in both endpoint images (BusyBox).
- The `campus-client` image includes `curl`; the sensor image has BusyBox
  `wget`/`ping` but no `curl`.

The lab's "Internet" is R2's loopback `8.8.8.8`. R2 has an HTTP listener on
port 80; there is no DNS or HTTPS service on the simulated Internet. Tests for
DNS/HTTPS therefore verify the ACL permit counters and the absence of a
listener, not a successful application response. This is called out explicitly
where it applies.

## 1. Requirement traceability

| Brief requirement | Tests |
|---|---|
| 2 routers and 3 switches | T01 |
| STAFF VLAN with at least 3 devices | T02, T04, T05, T11 |
| STUDENT VLAN with at least 3 devices | T02, T04, T06, T12 |
| GUEST VLAN with 1 guest | T02, T04, T06, T13 |
| IoT VLAN with at least 3 real sensors | T02, T04, T07, T14, T16 |
| Firewall policy | T11, T12, T13, T14, T15, T17 |
| Dynamic VLAN assignment via RADIUS | T05, T06, T07, T08 |
| Unauthenticated/failed auth fallback | T09, T10 |
| MQTT sensor traffic and isolation | T14, T16 |
| NAT/PAT and Internet access | T11, T12, T13, T18 |

## 2. Baseline tests

### T01 - Build inventory and link status

**Where:** GNS3 workspace; R1, R2, SW1-SW3 consoles.

**Steps:**

1. Confirm the GNS3 project contains R1, R2, SW1, SW2, SW3, seven client
   containers, three sensor containers, SERVER-CLOUD (16 nodes).
2. Confirm the 15 links in `topology/gns3-build-steps.md` section 5.
3. On R1 and each switch: `show cdp neighbors` (or `show lldp neighbors` if
   CDP is disabled).
4. On each device: `show ip interface brief`.

**Expected:** R1 sees SW1 on g0/0 and R2 on g0/2; SW1 sees SW2/SW3; every
configured interface is `up/up`; R1 g0/1 is up toward the Cloud.

**Evidence:** GNS3 topology screenshot, `show cdp neighbors` from R1, SW1,
`show ip interface brief` from all five devices.

### T02 - VLAN database and access-port membership

**Where:** SW1, SW2, SW3.

**Steps:**

```text
show vlan brief
show vlan id 10
show vlan id 20
show vlan id 30
show vlan id 40
show vlan id 99
```

**Expected:**

| Switch | VLAN 10 ports | VLAN 20 ports | VLAN 30 ports | VLAN 40 ports |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SW1 | none (trunks only) | none | none | none |
| SW2 | Gi0/1, Gi0/2, Gi0/3 | Gi1/0, Gi1/1, Gi1/2 | none | none |
| SW3 | none | none | Gi0/1 | Gi0/2, Gi0/3, Gi1/0 |

All five VLANs exist and have the names STAFF, STUDENT, GUEST, IOT, MGMT on
every switch. VLAN 99 has the management SVI.

> IOSvL2 has no `Gi0/4`-`Gi0/6`; student links 4-6 and the humidity sensor are
> on the `Gi1/x` port group. GNS3 adapter 4 maps to `Gi1/0`.
>
> After 802.1X succeeds, a port may be shown in the RADIUS-assigned VLAN
> instead of its initial access VLAN. Both should be the same VLAN in this
> design; T05/T06/T07 prove the assignment.

**Evidence:** `show vlan brief` from all three switches.

### T03 - Trunk status and allowed VLANs

**Where:** SW1, SW2, SW3.

**Steps:**

```text
show interfaces trunk
show interfaces GigabitEthernet0/0 switchport
```

**Expected:** SW1 has three trunk ports (g0/0, g0/1, g0/2); SW2 and SW3 each
have g0/0. Every trunk is `trunking`, `802.1q`, forwarding, and its allowed
VLAN list is exactly `10,20,30,40,99`. Native VLAN is 1. No access port appears
as a trunk.

**Evidence:** `show interfaces trunk` from each switch.

### T04 - Addressing and DHCP leases

**Where:** R1 and endpoints.

**Steps:**

1. On R1: `show ip interface brief`, `show ip dhcp binding`,
   `show ip dhcp pool`.
2. On each client/sensor: `ip addr show eth0`, `ip route`.
3. On R1: `show ip arp`.

**Expected:** R1 has 192.168.10.1, .20.1, .30.1, .40.1, .99.1, .50.1 and

matching default gateway and DNS 8.8.8.8. There are at least three STAFF
leases, three STUDENT leases, one GUEST lease and three IOT leases.

## 3. RADIUS dynamic VLAN tests

### T05 - staff1 is dynamically placed in VLAN 10

**Where:** STAFF-PC1, SW2, RADIUS logs.

**Preconditions:** STAFF-PC1 uses `wpa_supplicant-staff1.conf`; RADIUS is
running; SW2 g0/1 is connected.

**Steps:**

1. Reconnect/restart STAFF-PC1.
2. On SW2:

   ```text
   show authentication sessions
   show authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet0/1 details
   show dot1x interface GigabitEthernet0/1 details
   ```

3. On the Docker host, capture the RADIUS exchange in debug mode. Stop and
   remove the compose RADIUS container (this releases 192.168.50.10), start a
   debug instance on the same macvlan network, then trigger a reconnect:

   ```sh
   cd network-project/radius
   docker compose stop radius
   docker compose rm -f radius
   docker network ls | grep campus-network_server
   docker run --rm --network campus-network_server --ip 192.168.50.10 \
     -v "$PWD/clients.conf:/etc/freeradius/clients.conf:ro" \
     -v "$PWD/users:/etc/freeradius/mods-config/files/authorize:ro" \
     freeradius/freeradius-server:3.2.3 freeradius -X
   ```

   Press Ctrl-C when the exchange is captured, then restore the service with
   `docker compose up -d radius`. (The network name may be
   `campus-network_server` or `network-project_server` depending on the
   Compose project name.)

**Expected:** `show authentication sessions` shows interface g0/1, method
`dot1x`, status `Auth`, and **VLAN 10**. The RADIUS debug shows an
`Access-Accept` containing `Tunnel-Type = VLAN`,
`Tunnel-Medium-Type = IEEE-802`, and `Tunnel-Private-Group-Id = "10"`.
`show dot1x ... details` shows the supplicant MAC and `Authorized`.

**Evidence:** `show authentication sessions ... details`, the RADIUS
`Access-Accept` block, and the client's DHCP address in 192.168.10.0/24.

### T06 - student1 -> VLAN 20; guest1 -> VLAN 30

**Where:** STUDENT-PC1, GUEST-PC1, SW2 Gi1/0, SW3 Gi0/1.

**Steps:**

1. Reconnect STUDENT-PC1 with `wpa_supplicant-student1.conf`.
2. On SW2: `show authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet1/0 details`.
3. Reconnect GUEST-PC1 with `wpa_supplicant-guest1.conf`.
4. On SW3: `show authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet0/1 details`.

**Expected:** STUDENT-PC1 is authorized in VLAN 20 with a 192.168.20.x lease;
GUEST-PC1 is authorized in VLAN 30 with a 192.168.30.x lease. The RADIUS
Access-Accept for each contains the matching `Tunnel-Private-Group-Id`.

**Evidence:** Two session outputs, two DHCP addresses, RADIUS debug excerpts.

### T07 - Sensor access -> VLAN 40

**Where:** SW3 Gi0/2, Gi0/3, Gi1/0; RADIUS logs.

> **Platform note:** IOSvL2 accepts the `mab` command but never creates an
> authentication session, so a MAB-configured port stays unauthorized and the
> sensor cannot DHCP. The shipped `configs/SW3.cfg` pins each sensor MAC with
> port security instead. Both variants are checked below; on Catalyst hardware
> run the MAB variant, on IOSvL2 run the port-security variant.

**Steps (IOSvL2 / shipped config):**

1. Confirm each sensor's MAC:

   ```sh
   docker ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Image}}'
   docker exec <sensor-container> cat /sys/class/net/eth0/address
   ```

2. On SW3:

   ```text
   show port-security
   show port-security interface GigabitEthernet0/2
   show mac address-table | include 0200.0000.40
   ```

3. Confirm the sensors have 192.168.40.x leases (`ip addr show eth0` in each
   container) and publish to the broker (T16).

**Expected:** Each IoT port is `Secure-up`, maximum 1 address, `Restrict`,
with `Last Source Address:Vlan` equal to the sensor MAC in VLAN 40. The MAC
table shows the three addresses as `STATIC` in VLAN 40. Each sensor has a
192.168.40.x lease.

**Steps (hardware MAB variant):**

1. Replace the port-security lines on each IoT port with
   `authentication order mab`, `authentication port-control auto`, `mab` and
   `dot1x pae authenticator`.
2. `show authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet0/2 details` shows
   method `mab`, status `Auth`, VLAN 40.
3. In RADIUS debug, the Access-Request User-Name is `0200.0000.4001`
   (or one of the aliases in `radius/users`), and the Access-Accept contains
   `Tunnel-Private-Group-Id = "40"`.

**Evidence:** `report/evidence/T06-T07-sw3-sessions.txt` (port security,
sessions, MAC table), sensor leases, and `T16-mqtt-subscribe.txt`.

### T08 - Moving staff1 to another port keeps VLAN 10

**Where:** SW2 g0/1 and g0/3.

**Steps:**

1. With STAFF-PC1 authenticated on g0/1, delete the GNS3 link from SW2 g0/1.
2. Connect STAFF-PC1 itself to SW2 g0/3 (move its link), or use a spare client
   configured with the staff1 profile. Do not use STAFF-PC3's staff3 profile
   for this test.
3. If the port does not restart authentication, on SW2:

   ```text
   interface GigabitEthernet0/3
    shutdown
    no shutdown
   ```

4. Run `show authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet0/3 details`.

**Expected:** The new port authenticates the same staff1 identity and is
authorized in VLAN 10 with a 192.168.10.x address. The old port has no active
session. This proves the VLAN comes from RADIUS, not from the port's static
access VLAN (both staff ports start in VLAN 10, so also show the RADIUS
Access-Accept for the new session).

**Evidence:** Session output on g0/3, DHCP address, RADIUS debug for the new
NAS port.

### T09 - Wrong password -> guest fallback VLAN 30

**Where:** a spare client using `wpa_supplicant-wrongpass.conf`, SW2, RADIUS.

**Steps:**

1. Connect the spare client to a staff port (for example g0/2) with the
   wrong-password profile. Build/use a client image whose `WPA_CONF` points at
   `/etc/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant-wrongpass.conf`.
2. Watch `show authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet0/2 details`
   and the RADIUS debug.
3. Check the client's DHCP address: `ip addr show eth0`.

**Expected:** RADIUS returns `Access-Reject` for staff1. SW2 applies
`authentication event fail action authorize vlan 30`; the port is authorized
in **VLAN 30**, and the client gets a 192.168.30.x address. It can reach the
Internet but cannot ping 192.168.10.x, 192.168.40.x, 192.168.50.x or
192.168.99.x (guest ACL).

**Evidence:** Access-Reject, session output showing VLAN 30, guest DHCP lease,
failed internal pings.

### T10 - RADIUS server dead -> guest fallback VLAN 30

**Where:** STAFF-PC3 on SW2 `Gi0/3`, Docker host.

**Steps:**

1. Stop RADIUS: `docker stop radius` (or `docker compose stop radius`).
2. Force a fresh authentication attempt. Re-authentication on an already
   authorized port does not test this path, because IOS keeps the last known
   good session when a *re-auth* times out. Clear the session and restart
   EAPOL instead:
   - SW2: `clear authentication sessions interface GigabitEthernet0/3`
   - client: `wpa_cli -i eth0 reassociate`
     (or stop/start the endpoint in GNS3)
3. Wait for the dead criteria: `radius-server dead-criteria time 10 tries 2`
   with `timeout 5` / `retransmit 3` marks the server dead in roughly 30-60s.
4. Check `show aaa servers` (`Dead: ... count`), `show logging` for
   `%RADIUS-4-RADIUS_DEAD`, and
   `show interface GigabitEthernet0/3 switchport` (`Access Mode VLAN: 30`).
5. Renew DHCP on the client and test the guest ACL.
6. Restart RADIUS (`docker start radius`), clear the session and reassociate;
   confirm the port returns to VLAN 10.

**Expected:** While RADIUS is unreachable, the port is authorized in **VLAN 30**
by `authentication event server dead action authorize vlan 30`, and the client
gets a 192.168.30.x lease. As in T09, HTTP to 8.8.8.8 succeeds while staff,
RADIUS, MQTT and MGMT destinations are blocked by `GUEST_IN`.

**Note:** `authentication event no-response` is about a silent *supplicant*,
not a silent RADIUS server; it is not the right event for a RADIUS outage.
`authentication event server dead` is the working fallback on this image.

**Evidence:** `T10-server-dead.txt` - dead counter, `RADIUS_DEAD` syslog,
session in VLAN 30, 192.168.30.22 lease, HTTP 401, blocked internal probes.

## 4. Firewall policy tests

Run each row from the named endpoint. Use `ping` for ICMP rows and `curl` for
HTTP rows. A "pass" means the expected protocol succeeds; "fail" means it is
blocked by R1, not merely that an application is absent. For DNS and HTTPS,
there is no service on the simulated Internet, so the pass criterion is the
ACL permit counter incrementing (T17) rather than an application response.

### T11 - STAFF ACL matrix

**Where:** STAFF-PC1.

| # | Destination | Command | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8.8.8.8 | `ping -c 3 8.8.8.8` | Pass (NAT to Internet) |
| 2 | 8.8.8.8:80 | `curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://8.8.8.8/` | Pass (HTTP code, 401 is acceptable) |
| 3 | 192.168.50.10 | `ping -c 3 192.168.50.10` | Pass |
| 4 | 192.168.50.20 | `ping -c 3 192.168.50.20` | Pass |
| 5 | 192.168.20.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.20.21` | Pass |
| 6 | 192.168.40.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.40.21` | Pass |
| 7 | 192.168.99.11 | `ping -c 3 192.168.99.11` | Pass |
| 8 | 192.168.30.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.30.21` | Pass |

If a student/IoT/guest endpoint is not at `.21`, use its actual DHCP address
from T04. Staff has no deny rules, so all rows should succeed.

**Evidence:** Command output for all rows, `show access-lists` on R1 showing
STAFF_IN permit counters.

### T12 - STUDENT ACL matrix

**Where:** STUDENT-PC1.

| # | Destination | Command | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8.8.8.8 | `ping -c 3 8.8.8.8` | Fail (ICMP is not in the student allow-list; use HTTP row 2) |
| 2 | 8.8.8.8:80 | `curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://8.8.8.8/` | Pass (HTTP code) |
| 3 | 8.8.8.8:443 | `curl -k -sS -m 5 https://8.8.8.8/` | ACL permits; no HTTPS listener, so connection fails. Confirm STUDENT_IN permit counter increments. |
| 4 | 8.8.8.8:53 | `nslookup example.com 8.8.8.8` | ACL permits; no DNS listener, so timeout. Confirm permit counter increments. |
| 5 | 192.168.10.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.10.21` | Fail (STAFF denied) |
| 6 | 192.168.40.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.40.21` | Fail (IOT denied) |
| 7 | 192.168.99.11 | `ping -c 3 192.168.99.11` | Fail (MGMT denied) |
| 8 | 192.168.50.10 | `ping -c 3 192.168.50.10` | Fail (SERVER denied) |
| 9 | 192.168.50.20 | `ping -c 3 192.168.50.20` | Fail (SERVER/MQTT denied) |

> A ping between two hosts in VLAN 20 (for example student1 to student2) is
> **not** in this matrix. That traffic is switched by SW2 and never reaches
> R1's `STUDENT_IN` ACL, so it succeeds. The ACLs enforce inter-VLAN policy;
> same-VLAN peer isolation would require private VLANs or `switchport
> protected` on the access ports, which is outside this brief.

**Evidence:** Output for all rows; R1 `show access-lists` STUDENT_IN deny
counters for rows 5-9.

### T13 - GUEST ACL matrix

**Where:** GUEST-PC1.

| # | Destination | Command | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8.8.8.8 | `ping -c 3 8.8.8.8` | Fail (ICMP is not in the guest allow-list) |
| 2 | 8.8.8.8:80 | `curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://8.8.8.8/` | Pass (HTTP code) |
| 3 | 192.168.10.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.10.21` | Fail |
| 4 | 192.168.20.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.20.21` | Fail |
| 5 | 192.168.40.21 | `ping -c 3 192.168.40.21` | Fail |
| 6 | 192.168.50.10 | `ping -c 3 192.168.50.10` | Fail |
| 7 | 192.168.99.11 | `ping -c 3 192.168.99.11` | Fail |

**Evidence:** Output for all rows; GUEST_IN deny counters.

### T14 - IOT ACL matrix

**Where:** each sensor container (SENSOR-TEMP/MOTION/HUMIDITY), SW3.

| # | Destination | Command | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 192.168.50.20:1883 | MQTT publish is automatic; verify with T16 | Pass |
| 2 | 8.8.8.8 | `ping -c 3 8.8.8.8` | Fail (Internet denied) |
| 3 | 8.8.8.8:80 | `wget -T 5 -O /dev/null http://8.8.8.8/` | Fail (Internet denied) |
| 4 | 8.8.8.8:53 | `nslookup example.com 8.8.8.8` | ACL permits DNS; no DNS listener, so timeout. Confirm IOT_IN permit counter. |

IOT_IN counters showing 1883 permits and deny counters.

### T15 - MGMT ACL and RADIUS-only access

**Where:** SW2 (MGMT VLAN 99), R1.

**Steps:**

1. On SW2, test RADIUS reachability:

   ```text
   test aaa group CAMPUS-RADIUS staff1 Staff1Pass! legacy
   show radius statistics
   ```

2. Try to reach the Internet and MQTT from the switch's management SVI:

   ```text
   ping 8.8.8.8
   ping 192.168.50.20
   ```

3. Try to ping a staff endpoint from SW2:

   ```text
   ping 192.168.10.21
   ```

**Expected:** `test aaa` reports successful authentication (or at least a
RADIUS Access-Accept and non-zero auth counters); `show radius statistics`
shows requests/responses. Pings to 8.8.8.8, 192.168.50.20 and 192.168.10.21
fail (packets from VLAN 99 are denied by `MGMT_IN`). RADIUS still works because
UDP 1812/1813 to 192.168.50.10 is explicitly permitted.

> `MGMT_IN` also permits ICMP echo replies and established TCP so that staff
> (which `STAFF_IN` allows to reach MGMT) can ping or SSH to the switch SVIs.
> Switch-originated echo requests and TCP SYNs do not match those entries and
> are still denied, which is what this test checks.
>
> If `test aaa` is unsupported on your IOSvL2 image, the live 802.1X tests
> (T05-T09) already prove MGMT-to-RADIUS reachability; capture
> `show radius statistics` instead.

**Evidence:** `test aaa` output, `show radius statistics`, failed ping output,
MGMT_IN counters.

## 5. MQTT and sensor tests

### T16 - All three sensors publish to the broker

**Where:** Docker host, MQTT container.

**Steps:**

1. Confirm all three sensor containers are running and have 192.168.40.x
   addresses.
2. Subscribe for at least 9 messages (3 sensors x 3 samples at 5-second
   intervals):

   ```sh
   docker exec -it mqtt mosquitto_sub \
     -h 127.0.0.1 -t 'campus/iot/#' -v -C 9
   ```

3. Save the output. Each line should be `campus/iot/<id> {"id":...}`.

**Expected:** Messages from `temp-01`, `motion-01` and `humidity-01` arrive
within 30 seconds. Payloads are JSON with `id`, `type`, `value`, `timestamp`;
types are `temperature`, `motion`, `humidity`; values are plausible (18-26,
0/1, 35-65). No sensor can ping 8.8.8.8 (T14 row 2), proving the IoT ACL does
not accidentally permit general Internet access.

**Evidence:** `mosquitto_sub` output with at least 9 lines, sensor logs,
sensor `ip addr`, failed Internet ping from one sensor.

### T17 - ACL hit counters

**Where:** R1.

**Steps:**

1. Before tests: `clear ip access-list counters` (or note the current counts).
2. Run the T11-T15 matrix.
3. `show access-lists`.
4. `show logging | include ACL|denied` (the ACL entries use `log`).

**Expected:** `STAFF_IN` has high permit counts and no denies; `STUDENT_IN`,
`GUEST_IN`, `IOT_IN` and `MGMT_IN` each show both permits for allowed traffic
and nonzero denies for the blocked rows. The final `deny ip any any log` entry
has a nonzero count when a test hit an unlisted destination. Log entries show
the source/destination and the ACL name.

**Evidence:** `show access-lists` before/after, `show logging` excerpt.

### T18 - NAT/PAT

**Where:** R1, STAFF-PC1/STUDENT-PC1/GUEST-PC1.

**Steps:**

1. From STAFF-PC1, `ping -c 3 8.8.8.8`.
2. From STUDENT-PC1 and GUEST-PC1, use
   `curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://8.8.8.8/`
   (their ACLs do not permit ICMP).
3. On R1: `show ip nat translations`, `show ip nat statistics`.
4. From an IoT sensor, attempt `ping 8.8.8.8`, then check NAT again.

**Expected:** Staff, student and guest flows appear as translations from
10.0.0.1 to 8.8.8.8; IoT produces no translation because its ACL drops the
packet before NAT. Server/MGMT traffic is not translated.

**Evidence:** NAT translation table, NAT statistics, IoT failed ping.

## 6. Supporting tests

### T19 - Spanning tree

**Where:** SW1, SW2, SW3.

show spanning-tree vlan 20

**Evidence:** `show startup-config` excerpts, post-reload session output.

# Report Outline

Use this as the structure for the written submission. The report should read
as a design-and-verification document, not as a list of commands. Put the raw
evidence in an appendix or in `report/evidence/`, and reference each item from
the relevant section.

## Title page

- Project title: **Segmented Campus Network with Firewall Policy and RADIUS
  Dynamic VLAN Assignment**
- Course/module, student name, date
- One-line scope statement: two routers, three switches, four user VLANs, an
  out-of-band management VLAN, a server segment, 802.1X/MAB, and an ACL
  firewall on R1.

## 1. Executive summary (1 page)

- What was built.
- How the brief is met: VLANs and device counts, firewall policy, RADIUS
  dynamic VLAN, IoT/MQTT.
- Headline test results (for example "all 20 tests passed except ...").
- The most important limitation: IOSvL2 802.1X/emulation caveats and the
  simulated Internet/DNS service.

## 2. Requirements and design decisions

- Restate the brief (a) VLAN segmentation and (b) firewall + dynamic VLAN.
- Explain the fixed design choices:
  - router-on-a-stick on R1 g0/0;
  - IOSvL2 access switches;
  - R1 as DHCP/NAT/firewall;
  - RADIUS and MQTT on an isolated server segment;
  - MGMT VLAN 99 for switch/radius control traffic;
  - 802.1X for user ports, MAB for headless sensors;
  - EAP-MD5 because stock FreeRADIUS supports it without certificates.
- State what is out of scope: real Internet, DNS service, production PKI,
  redundancy/HA, wireless.

## 3. Topology and physical/logical design

Include:

- GNS3 topology screenshot with all nodes and link labels.
- Logical diagram (VLANs/trunks/server segment).
- Node inventory table.
- Port map table (from `topology/topology.md`).
- Explanation of why SW1 is the spanning-tree root and why the server segment
  is routed rather than trunked.
- The Cloud/macvlan/veth plumbing for RADIUS and MQTT (one short paragraph and
  a simple diagram). Explain that R1, not Docker, is the server gateway.

**Screenshots/evidence:**

1. GNS3 workspace, zoomed to show node names and all links.
2. `show cdp neighbors` on R1 and SW1.
3. A photo/screenshot of the server-segment diagram from
   `topology/topology.md`.

## 4. Addressing and VLAN plan

Include the tables for:

- VLAN ID/name/subnet/gateway/DHCP range.
- Management addresses.
- R1-R2 link and 8.8.8.8 loopback.
- Server segment addresses.
- Fixed sensor MACs.

Explain:

- Why `.1-.20` are excluded from DHCP.
- Why VLAN 99 is management-only.
- Why the server segment is not NATed.
- How DHCP selects a pool on a router-on-a-stick subinterface.

**Screenshots/evidence:**

1. `show ip interface brief` on R1.
2. `show vlan brief` on SW1/SW2/SW3 (three screenshots).
3. `show ip dhcp binding` on R1.
4. `ip addr`/`ip route` on one endpoint per VLAN.

## 5. Layer 2 design and 802.1X/MAB

Explain:

- Trunk allowed lists and native VLAN choice.
- Access-port initial VLANs and dynamic VLAN override.
- `spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst`, SW1 root.
- 802.1X authenticator roles on SW2/SW3.
- MAB on IoT ports.
- Why IoT MAB failure is not sent to the guest VLAN (security rationale).
- Fallback behavior on user ports: `fail` and `no-response` -> VLAN 30.

**Screenshots/evidence:**

1. `show interfaces trunk` (all three switches).
2. `show spanning-tree vlan 10` on SW1 and SW2.
3. `show authentication sessions` on SW2 before/after a client connects.
4. `show dot1x all` on SW3.
5. The switch port block from `configs/SW2.cfg` and `configs/SW3.cfg` (code
   listing, not a screenshot).

## 6. RADIUS design and dynamic VLAN flow

Include a sequence diagram:

```
Supplicant --EAPOL--> Switch --RADIUS Access-Request--> FreeRADIUS
Supplicant <--EAP-- Switch <--Access-Accept (Tunnel-* attributes)-- FreeRADIUS
Switch applies Tunnel-Private-Group-Id, port moves to VLAN
```

Explain:

- `aaa new-model`, `aaa authentication dot1x`, `aaa authorization network`,
  `aaa accounting dot1x`.
- `radius server` entry, the named `CAMPUS-RADIUS` server group, `ip radius
  source-interface Vlan99`, shared secret.
- `clients.conf` entries for SW1/SW2/SW3.
- `users` entries: staff/student/guest and MAC users.
- The three Tunnel attributes and why `aaa authorization network` is required.
- EAP-MD5 trade-off versus PEAP/MSCHAPv2.
- How to change the shared secret consistently.

**Screenshots/evidence:**

1. `radiusd -X` Access-Accept for staff1, student1, guest1 and one MAC user,
   with the Tunnel attributes visible.
2. `show authentication sessions ... details` showing VLAN 10/20/30/40.
3. `show radius statistics` on SW2/SW3.
4. `clients.conf` and `users` excerpts.

## 7. Firewall policy and ACL rationale

Include the policy table from the brief and the implemented ACL table. For each
ACL explain:

- Direction: inbound on the R1 subinterface, so it filters client-originated
  traffic before routing.
- Ordering: DHCP/DNS/HTTP permits relative to the RFC1918 denies; MQTT permit
  before the 192.168/16 deny.
- Why `deny ip any any log` is explicit.
- Why `established` and echo-reply rules are present for return traffic while
  the policy remains one-way for new sessions.
- Why the server subnet and MGMT are not NATed.
- Why NAT is not a security control by itself.

Also discuss what a production design would add: stateful zone firewall,
default-deny on the server segment, RADIUS CoA, DHCP snooping/DAI, port
security, private VLAN/port isolation for same-VLAN peers, and logging to a
collector.

**Screenshots/evidence:**

1. `show access-lists` on R1 with counters after the matrix.
2. `show ip nat translations`.
3. `show logging` excerpt for a denied flow.
4. A table of actual pass/fail results copied from the test plan.

## 8. IoT and MQTT design

Explain:

- Three Docker sensors, one per type, publishing JSON every 5 seconds.
- Topic scheme `campus/iot/<id>`.
- Broker at 192.168.50.20, anonymous lab access.
- IoT ACL: DHCP, DNS to 8.8.8.8, MQTT 1883 to the broker, everything else
  denied.
- Why MAB is appropriate for headless devices and why the MAC is the identity.
- The MAC-format caveat.

**Screenshots/evidence:**

1. `docker ps` showing three sensor containers.
2. Sensor log showing published JSON.
3. `mosquitto_sub` output with all three sensor IDs.
4. Failed `ping 8.8.8.8` from a sensor.
5. `show authentication sessions` for the three IoT ports.

## 9. Test methodology and results

- State that testing was performed in GNS3; include GNS3 version, image
  versions, host OS and Docker version.
- Summarize the test plan: 20 tests, grouped by baseline, RADIUS, firewall,
  MQTT, supporting.
- Include the pass/fail summary sheet.
- For each failed or partially verified test, explain the cause and whether it
  is a design issue or an emulator/service limitation.
- Include the offline checks: `python3 tests/verify_configs.py` output,
  `freeradius -CX`, `docker compose config`, and the MQTT local test.

**Screenshots/evidence:**

1. `verify_configs.py` final output (0 failed).
2. `docker compose ps`.
3. `freeradius -CX` output.
4. The completed pass/fail sheet.

## 10. Limitations and threats to validity

State clearly:

- IOSvL2 802.1X can be flaky or unavailable depending on the image/feature
  set. If it was unavailable, the fallback was MAB-only and the report must say
  so; this still demonstrates RADIUS VLAN assignment but not EAP.
- GNS3 is not a production switch; timing, MAC learning and EAPOL behavior
  differ from hardware.
- EAP-MD5 is lab-only; production should use PEAP/MSCHAPv2 or EAP-TLS.
- The simulated Internet is R2 8.8.8.8; HTTP is available but DNS/HTTPS are not.
  DNS/HTTPS tests therefore verify ACL permits, not application success.
- Anonymous MQTT and a shared RADIUS secret are lab choices, not production
  security.
- The RADIUS/MQTT containers are external to GNS3 and depend on the host
  bridge/macvlan setup; a GNS3 VM needs the same plumbing inside the VM.
- Offline checks cannot prove Cisco IOS syntax or end-to-end behavior.

## 11. Conclusion

- Re-state how the brief is satisfied.
- What was learned about segmentation, 802.1X/MAB, RADIUS attributes, and
  firewall ordering.
- What would be improved in a second iteration (stateful firewall, CoA,
  PEAP/EAP-TLS, redundant links, monitoring).

## Appendix A - Full configurations

Include the five files from `configs/` as code listings. Do not paste
screenshots of configs; text is easier to mark.

## Appendix B - RADIUS files

`clients.conf`, `users` (redact the shared secret/passwords if the report is
public), and `secrets.env` key names.

## Appendix C - Evidence index

| Figure | File | Captured from | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `T01-topology.png` | GNS3 | T01 |
| 2 | `T02-show-vlan-sw1.png` | SW1 | T02 |
| ... | ... | ... | ... |

## Appendix D - Command reference

The exact verification commands used, copied from `tests/test-plan.md`:

```text
show vlan brief
show interfaces trunk
show ip interface brief
show ip dhcp binding
show authentication sessions
show authentication sessions interface <port> details
show dot1x all
show access-lists
show ip nat translations
show radius statistics
show spanning-tree vlan 10
```

## Screenshot checklist (minimum)

- [ ] GNS3 topology with all nodes and links
- [ ] `show vlan brief` x3 switches
- [ ] `show interfaces trunk` x3 switches
- [ ] `show spanning-tree vlan 10` on SW1 and SW2
- [ ] `show authentication sessions` for staff1, student1, guest1
- [ ] `show authentication sessions` for the three sensor MACs
- [ ] staff1 moved to a second port, still VLAN 10
- [ ] wrong password -> VLAN 30
- [ ] RADIUS stopped -> VLAN 30
- [ ] RADIUS debug Access-Accept with all three Tunnel attributes
- [ ] RADIUS debug Access-Reject for the wrong password
- [ ] `show ip dhcp binding` per VLAN
- [ ] ACL matrix command outputs (pass and fail rows)
- [ ] `show access-lists` counters
- [ ] `show ip nat translations`
- [ ] `mosquitto_sub` output from all three sensors
- [ ] sensor failed Internet ping
- [ ] `verify_configs.py` 0 failures
- [ ] `freeradius -CX` success
- [ ] `docker compose ps` healthy

# Live Test Results

Run on the GNS3 3.1 project `campus-network` (16 nodes, 15 links) with
IOSv/IOSvL2 images, FreeRADIUS 3.2.3 and Mosquitto 2.x. Console output and
command transcripts are in `report/evidence/`.

## Summary sheet

| Test | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| T01 Build inventory | Pass | `T01-T20-r1.txt`, `T02-T03-T19-sw1.txt` |
| T02 VLAN membership | Pass | `T02-T03-T19-sw1.txt`, `T02-T19-sw2.txt`, `T02-T19-sw3.txt` |

| T06 student1/guest1 VLANs | Pass | `T05-T15-sw2-sessions.txt`, `T06-T07-sw3-sessions.txt` |
| T07 Sensor access VLAN 40 | Pass (port security; see limitation) | `T06-T07-sw3-sessions.txt`, `T16-mqtt-subscribe.txt` |

| T11 STAFF ACL matrix | Pass | `T11-staff-acl-matrix.txt` |
| T12 STUDENT ACL matrix | Pass | `T12-student-acl-matrix.txt` |
| T13 GUEST ACL matrix | Pass | `T13-guest-acl-matrix.txt` |
| T14 IOT ACL matrix | Pass | `T14-iot-acl-matrix.txt` |
| T15 MGMT RADIUS-only | Pass | `T05-T15-sw2-sessions.txt` |
| T16 MQTT all sensors | Pass | `T16-mqtt-subscribe.txt` |
| T17 ACL counters | Pass | `T17-T18-r1-acl-nat.txt` |
| T18 NAT/PAT | Pass | `T18-nat-live.txt` |
| T19 Spanning tree | Pass | `T02-T03-T19-sw1.txt` and SW2/SW3 files |
| T20 Config persistence | Partial | `T01-T20-r1.txt`, startup hostname checks on all five devices |

## Key observations

### 802.1X dynamic VLAN

- `SW2 Gi0/1` staff1: `dot1x Authc Success`, server policy `Vlan: 10`,
  lease 192.168.10.21.
- `SW2 Gi1/0` student1: `Authc Success`, `Vlan: 20`, lease 192.168.20.21.
- `SW3 Gi0/1` guest1: `Authc Success`, `Vlan: 30`, lease 192.168.30.21.
- `test aaa group CAMPUS-RADIUS staff1 Staff1Pass! legacy` returns
  `User was successfully authenticated`; `show radius statistics` shows 13
  auth responses, 0 timeouts.

### IoT access (platform limitation)

MAB is not usable on IOSvL2. With `mab` configured, the sensor's DHCP
discovers arrive on `Gi0/2` (link capture and interface counters both show
them), but `show authentication sessions` stays empty and the MAC table never
learns the address, because the 802.1X-controlled port discards data frames
until authorized. `debug mab all` / `debug authentication all` produce no
events.

The shipped config pins the sensor MAC with port security:

```
show port-security
Secure Port  MaxSecureAddr  CurrentAddr  SecurityViolation  Security Action
      Gi0/2              1            1                  0         Restrict
      Gi0/3              1            1                  0         Restrict
      Gi1/0              1            1                  0         Restrict
```

All three sensors then obtain 192.168.40.21-23 and publish to the broker.
RADIUS is still MAB-ready: `radtest 0200.0000.4001` returns Access-Accept with
`Tunnel-Private-Group-Id = "40"`.

### Failed-auth fallback (T09)

STAFF-PC2 was restarted with `wpa_supplicant-wrongpass.conf` on `Gi0/2`.
RADIUS rejected staff1 three times, SW2 logged `DOT1X-5-RESULT_OVERRIDE` and
applied `AUTH_FAIL_VLAN_Gi0/2` with `Vlan: 30`. A manual `udhcpc` on that
container obtained 192.168.30.22; HTTP to 8.8.8.8 returned 401 while pings to
192.168.10.21, 192.168.40.21 and 192.168.50.10 were dropped by the guest ACL.
The node was then restored to the staff2 profile and re-authenticated in VLAN
10 with 192.168.10.22.

### RADIUS server dead (T10)

The first attempt used `authentication event no-response`, which is the
*supplicant silent* event; it does not fire when RADIUS is unreachable. The
working configuration is `authentication event server dead action authorize
vlan 30`, plus `radius-server dead-criteria time 10 tries 2`.

With the RADIUS container stopped, the session cleared and a fresh EAPOL
exchange, SW2 logged `%RADIUS-4-RADIUS_DEAD` and the `Dead: ... count`
incremented. `Gi0/3` was authorized in VLAN 30 (`UNKNOWN Auth` session) and
STAFF-PC3 obtained 192.168.30.22. HTTP to 8.8.8.8 returned 401 (the simulated
Internet listener), while pings to 192.168.10.21 and TCP to 192.168.50.10/20
were dropped by `GUEST_IN`. After RADIUS restarted and the session was
cleared, the port returned to VLAN 10 and the client renewed 192.168.10.23.

Two operational notes:

- A *re-authentication* timeout does not move an already authorized port; IOS
  keeps the last known good session. T10 needs a fresh session (clear the
  session / bounce the link).
- The default dead criteria are slow (10 tries). The lab sets `time 10 tries 2`
  so the fallback happens in under a minute.

The same `server dead` policy is applied to every 802.1X user port on SW2 and
to the guest port on SW3.

### ACL and NAT

- `STAFF_IN` 58 matches, 0 denies; all eight staff rows succeed, including
  Internet HTTP 401 and ping to the SW1 SVI.
- `STUDENT_IN` and `GUEST_IN`: HTTP to 8.8.8.8 succeeds (401); pings to staff,
  IoT, MGMT, RADIUS and MQTT fail with 100% loss; deny counters increase.
- `IOT_IN`: 605 matches on `tcp ... 192.168.50.20 eq 1883`; Internet and

display.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Publish fake IoT sensor readings to the campus MQTT broker.

Environment variables:
  SENSOR_ID         unique id, e.g. temp-01
  SENSOR_TYPE       temperature | motion | humidity
  MQTT_BROKER       default 192.168.50.20
  MQTT_PORT         default 1883
  PUBLISH_INTERVAL  seconds, default 5
  MQTT_TOPIC        default campus/iot/<SENSOR_ID>
"""

import json
import os
import random
import signal
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt

BROKER = os.getenv("MQTT_BROKER", "192.168.50.20")
PORT = int(os.getenv("MQTT_PORT", "1883"))
SENSOR_ID = os.getenv("SENSOR_ID", "sensor-01")
SENSOR_TYPE = os.getenv("SENSOR_TYPE", "temperature").strip().lower()
INTERVAL = float(os.getenv("PUBLISH_INTERVAL", "5"))
TOPIC = os.getenv("MQTT_TOPIC", f"campus/iot/{SENSOR_ID}")

ALLOWED_TYPES = {"temperature", "motion", "humidity"}
if SENSOR_TYPE not in ALLOWED_TYPES:
    print(
        f"[{SENSOR_ID}] WARNING: SENSOR_TYPE={SENSOR_TYPE!r} is not one of "
        f"{sorted(ALLOWED_TYPES)}; falling back to temperature",
        flush=True,
    )
    SENSOR_TYPE = "temperature"

_stop = False


def _handle_signal(signum, _frame):
    global _stop
    _stop = True
    print(f"[{SENSOR_ID}] received signal {signum}, stopping", flush=True)


def make_reading():
    if SENSOR_TYPE == "temperature":
        value = round(random.uniform(18.0, 26.0), 2)
    elif SENSOR_TYPE == "humidity":
        value = round(random.uniform(35.0, 65.0), 2)
    else:  # motion
        value = random.choice([0, 1])
    return {
        "id": SENSOR_ID,
        "type": SENSOR_TYPE,
        "value": value,
        "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"),
    }


def connect_with_retry():
    client = mqtt.Client(
        mqtt.CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION2,
        client_id=SENSOR_ID,
        clean_session=True,
    )
    client.reconnect_delay_set(min_delay=1, max_delay=30)
    while not _stop:
        try:
            print(f"[{SENSOR_ID}] connecting to {BROKER}:{PORT}", flush=True)
            client.connect(BROKER, PORT, keepalive=60)
            return client
        except OSError as exc:
            print(f"[{SENSOR_ID}] connect failed: {exc}; retrying in 5s", flush=True)
            time.sleep(5)
    return client


def main():
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _handle_signal)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _handle_signal)

    print(
        f"[{SENSOR_ID}] type={SENSOR_TYPE} topic={TOPIC} "
        f"broker={BROKER}:{PORT} interval={INTERVAL}s",
        flush=True,
    )

    client = connect_with_retry()
    if _stop:
        return 0
    client.loop_start()

    try:
        while not _stop:
            payload = make_reading()
            body = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"))
            result = client.publish(TOPIC, body, qos=1)
            try:
                result.wait_for_publish(timeout=5)
            except RuntimeError:
                pass

            if result.rc == mqtt.MQTT_ERR_SUCCESS:
                print(f"[{SENSOR_ID}] published {body}", flush=True)
            else:
                print(
                    f"[{SENSOR_ID}] publish failed rc={result.rc}; "
                    "will keep trying",
                    flush=True,
                )

            slept = 0.0
            while slept < INTERVAL and not _stop:
                time.sleep(min(1.0, INTERVAL - slept))
                slept += 1.0
    finally:
        client.loop_stop()
        client.disconnect()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

display.text:
#!/bin/sh
# Sensor container startup: optional MAC override, DHCP, then MQTT loop.
set -eu

# MAB is keyed on the source MAC. Prefer setting the MAC in the GNS3 Docker
# node properties; SENSOR_MAC is a fallback for images/containers that have
# NET_ADMIN. If the set fails, the container keeps the MAC Docker/GNS3 gave it.
#
# SENSOR_MAC uses the Cisco dotted form (0200.0000.4001), but Linux `ip link`
# needs colon-separated hex (02:00:00:00:40:01). Normalise either form, and
# bounce the link so the switch starts MAB with the new MAC.
if [ -n "${SENSOR_MAC:-}" ]; then
    MAC_HEX=$(printf '%s' "$SENSOR_MAC" | tr 'A-F' 'a-f' | tr -d '.:-')
    case "$MAC_HEX" in
        *[!0-9a-f]*|"")
            echo "[entrypoint] WARNING: SENSOR_MAC=$SENSOR_MAC is not a 12-digit hex MAC; ignoring"
            ;;
        *)
            if [ "${#MAC_HEX}" -ne 12 ]; then
                echo "[entrypoint] WARNING: SENSOR_MAC=$SENSOR_MAC is not a 12-digit hex MAC; ignoring"
            else
                MAC_COLON=$(printf '%s' "$MAC_HEX" | sed 's/../&:/g; s/:$//')
                ip link set dev eth0 down 2>/dev/null || true
                if ip link set dev eth0 address "$MAC_COLON" 2>/dev/null; then
                    echo "[entrypoint] eth0 MAC set to $MAC_COLON"
                else
                    echo "[entrypoint] WARNING: could not set eth0 MAC to $MAC_COLON"
                    echo "[entrypoint] current MAC: $(cat /sys/class/net/eth0/address 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
                fi
                ip link set dev eth0 up 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            ;;
    esac
fi

if [ "${SENSOR_DHCP:-1}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[entrypoint] requesting DHCP on eth0"
    udhcpc -i eth0 -s /app/udhcpc.script -t 30 -T 3 -q -n -f || {
        echo "[entrypoint] WARNING: DHCP did not complete; continuing anyway"
    }
fi

exec python -u /app/sensor.py

#!/bin/sh
# 802.1X supplicant + DHCP client for a wired GNS3 Docker endpoint.
set -eu

CONF="${WPA_CONF:-/etc/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant-staff1.conf}"
NAME="${CLIENT_NAME:-client}"
LOG=/tmp/wpa_supplicant.log
mkdir -p /var/run/wpa_supplicant
: > "$LOG"

echo "[$NAME] using supplicant config $CONF"
echo "[$NAME] MAC before 802.1X: $(cat /sys/class/net/eth0/address 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"

# The wired driver is the correct one for an Ethernet port. Fall back to wext
# only for unusual images; wired is what IOSvL2 expects.
# Note: wpa_supplicant 2.10 has no -f option; redirect its output instead.
if ! wpa_supplicant -i eth0 -D wired -c "$CONF" -B >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
    echo "[$NAME] wired driver failed, retrying with wext"
    wpa_supplicant -i eth0 -D wext -c "$CONF" -B >>"$LOG" 2>&1 || true
fi

# Give the switch and RADIUS time to finish EAP before asking for DHCP. If the
# authentication fails and the switch applies the guest fallback VLAN, udhcpc
# still retries long enough to obtain a lease in VLAN 30.
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do
    STATE=$(wpa_cli -i eth0 status 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^wpa_state=//p')
    echo "[$NAME] wpa_state=${STATE:-unknown}"
    [ "$STATE" = "COMPLETED" ] && break
    sleep 2
done

echo "[$NAME] requesting DHCP"
udhcpc -i eth0 -s /usr/local/bin/udhcpc.script -t 30 -T 3 -q -n -f || {
    echo "[$NAME] WARNING: no DHCP lease yet; leaving container running"
}

echo "[$NAME] interface state:"
ip addr show eth0 || true

# Keep the container alive and stream supplicant state to the GNS3 console.
exec tail -f "$LOG"

1: # GNS3 Build Steps
2: 
3: These are click-by-click steps for GNS3 2.2.x on Linux. GNS3 is not run by the
4: person who generated this repo, so treat the GUI labels as a guide: wording
5: changes slightly between GNS3 releases. The configs and topology are the
6: authoritative parts.
7: 
8: ## 0. What you must supply
9: 
10: The repo does **not** contain Cisco images. You must obtain them yourself and
11: comply with Cisco's licence terms:
12: 
13: - A Cisco **IOSv** image for R1 and R2 (IOS 15.x, at least 3 GigabitEthernet
14:   interfaces). Import it as a QEMU IOSv template.
15: - A Cisco **IOSvL2** image for SW1, SW2 and SW3 (IOS 15.2, at least 8
16:   GigabitEthernet interfaces, 802.1X capable). Import it as a QEMU IOSvL2
17:   template and mark it as an Ethernet switch.
18: 
19: The configs use the port names of the IOSvL2 image that this lab was built
20: and tested on: `GigabitEthernet0/0`-`0/3` and `GigabitEthernet1/0`-`1/3`.
21: IOSvL2 has **no** `Gi0/4`-`Gi0/6`; the fifth to seventh access links land on
22: `Gi1/0`-`Gi1/2`. GNS3 adapter 0-3 maps to `Gi0/0`-`Gi0/3`, adapter 4-7 maps to
23: `Gi1/0`-`Gi1/3`. Router ports are `Gi0/0`-`Gi0/2` on IOSv.
24: 
25: You also need:
26: 
27: - Docker Engine with Compose v2, on the same Linux host as the GNS3 server (or
28:   inside the GNS3 VM if that is where the server runs).
29: - The `campus-client:1.0` and `campus-sensor:1.0` images built in step 2.
30: - Internet access only for the first image pulls/builds. The lab itself uses
31:   the simulated 8.8.8.8 host on R2.
32: 
33: ## 1. Prepare the Docker server segment first
34: 
35: The RADIUS and MQTT containers must be running before the switches boot,
36: otherwise the first 802.1X attempts time out (the switches will use the guest
37: fallback, but the demonstration is cleaner if RADIUS is ready).
38: 
39: ```sh
40: cd network-project/radius
41: chmod +x setup-server-bridge.sh
42: ./setup-server-bridge.sh
43: docker compose up -d
44: docker compose ps
45: docker logs radius --tail 30
46: ```
47: 
48: Wait for the FreeRADIUS log line `Ready to process requests`. If you see
49: `Error binding to port` or a config error, stop here and fix it before building
50: the topology. `docker logs mqtt` should show `mosquitto version ... running`.
51: 
52: The setup script creates:
53: 
54: - `br-srv`: the Linux bridge that the GNS3 Cloud node attaches to.
55: - `srv-mac` / `srv-br`: a veth pair; `srv-mac` is the macvlan parent used by
56:   Compose, `srv-br` is enslaved to `br-srv`.
57: 
58: If your GNS3 server is in a **GNS3 VM**, run these commands inside that VM.
59: The Cloud node must be able to see `br-srv` on the GNS3 server host. A local
60: GNS3 server on the same Linux host is the simplest setup.
61: 
62: ## 2. Build the endpoint images
63: 
64: From the repo root:
65: 
66: ```sh
67: docker build -t campus-client:1.0 endpoints/client
68: docker build -t campus-sensor:1.0 endpoints/sensor
69: docker images | grep campus
70: ```
71: 
72: `campus-client` contains all seven supplicant profiles. The profile is selected
73: at runtime with `WPA_CONF`; do not build a separate image per user.
74: 
75: ## 3. Create the GNS3 project and templates
76: 
77: 1. Start GNS3 and create a new blank project named `campus-network`.
78: 2. Open **Edit > Preferences > QEMU > IOS routers** (or the equivalent
79:    template manager) and import your IOSv image. Name the template `IOSv`.
80:    Set RAM to at least 512 MB. Set **Adapters** to **3** (R1 needs g0/0, g0/1,
81:    g0/2).
82: 3. Import your IOSvL2 image as template `IOSvL2`. Set RAM to at least 512 MB.
83:    Set **Adapters** to **5** (SW2 needs five switch ports: `Gi0/0`-`Gi0/3` for
84:    the trunk and three staff PCs, plus `Gi1/0` for the first student PC) - or
85:    keep 8, which is what the tested project uses. Mark the template as an
86:    Ethernet switch if GNS3 offers that option.
87: 4. Open **Edit > Preferences > Docker > Docker containers > New**. Create:
88:    - `campus-client`: image `campus-client:1.0`, 1 adapter.
89:    - `campus-sensor`: image `campus-sensor:1.0`, 1 adapter.
90:    Accept the default console settings unless your GNS3 version requires a
91:    specific console type. Both images are intentionally long-running.
92: 5. Make sure the GNS3 **Cloud** node is available (it is under End devices).
93: 
94: ## 4. Place the nodes
95: 
96: Drag these into the workspace and rename them exactly:
97: 
98: - R1, R2 (IOSv)
99: - SW1, SW2, SW3 (IOSvL2)
100: - STAFF-PC1, STAFF-PC2, STAFF-PC3 (campus-client)
101: - STUDENT-PC1, STUDENT-PC2, STUDENT-PC3 (campus-client)
102: - GUEST-PC1 (campus-client)
103: - SENSOR-TEMP, SENSOR-MOTION, SENSOR-HUMIDITY (campus-sensor)
104: - SERVER-CLOUD (Cloud)
105: 
106: A suggested layout is in `topology/topology.md`. Node positions do not affect
107: the configuration.
108: 
109: ## 5. Cable the links
110: 
111: Use the Link tool and connect exactly these ports. GNS3 may label the Docker
112: side `eth0`; that is correct.
113: 
114: | # | From | To |
115: |---|---|---|
116: | 1 | R1 g0/0 | SW1 g0/0 |
117: | 2 | SW1 g0/1 | SW2 g0/0 |
118: | 3 | SW1 g0/2 | SW3 g0/0 |
119: | 4 | SW2 g0/1 | STAFF-PC1 eth0 |
120: | 5 | SW2 g0/2 | STAFF-PC2 eth0 |
121: | 6 | SW2 g0/3 | STAFF-PC3 eth0 |
122: | 7 | SW2 Gi1/0 | STUDENT-PC1 eth0 |
123: | 8 | SW2 Gi1/1 | STUDENT-PC2 eth0 |
124: | 9 | SW2 Gi1/2 | STUDENT-PC3 eth0 |
125: | 10 | SW3 Gi0/1 | GUEST-PC1 eth0 |
126: | 11 | SW3 Gi0/2 | SENSOR-TEMP eth0 |
127: | 12 | SW3 Gi0/3 | SENSOR-MOTION eth0 |
128: | 13 | SW3 Gi1/0 | SENSOR-HUMIDITY eth0 |
129: | 14 | R1 g0/1 | SERVER-CLOUD |
130: | 15 | R1 g0/2 | R2 g0/0 |
131: 
132: For link 14, right-click the Cloud node, choose **Configure**, and select
133: `br-srv` as the interface. If your GNS3 build lists bridges only after a
134: refresh, restart the GNS3 server once and reopen the project.
135: 
136: ## 6. Configure the Docker endpoints
137: 
138: ### 6.1 Sensor nodes
139: 
140: Open each sensor node's configuration and set the environment variables:
141: 
142: | Node | `SENSOR_ID` | `SENSOR_TYPE` | `SENSOR_MAC` |
143: |---|---|---|---|
144: | SENSOR-TEMP | `temp-01` | `temperature` | `0200.0000.4001` |
145: | SENSOR-MOTION | `motion-01` | `motion` | `0200.0000.4002` |
146: | SENSOR-HUMIDITY | `humidity-01` | `humidity` | `0200.0000.4003` |

148: The sensor MACs must match both the SW3 port-security entry and `radius/users`.
149: Prefer the GNS3 Docker node's **MAC address** field if your version offers one;
150: that field normally expects the colon form (`02:00:00:00:40:01`), while
151: `SENSOR_MAC` accepts the dotted form in the table. Otherwise the container
152: entrypoint normalises the dotted `SENSOR_MAC` value to `02:00:00:00:40:01`,

186: 1. **Docker server segment** (step 1): RADIUS and MQTT first.

218: - `switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q` is accepted on most IOSvL2 images. If
219:   your image rejects it (some L2-only images only support dot1q and have no
